title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
先二月至永懐時屆允㲉
勤用休于資迺若總理河道
右副都御史郭〔持平〕撫
陽右僉都御史戴〔時宗〕監祭
御史巡鹽〔舒遷〕党〔承賜〕印馬
黎〔循典〕咸賛厥成右布
查〔應兆〕左叅政胡〔體乾〕
===
政王〔慎中〕劉〔友仁〕左叅
良〔傅〕右叅議左〔傑〕王〔傅〕
王〔家〕湯〔紹恩〕端〔廷赦〕張〔素〕僉
事張〔晃〕林〔雲同〕趙〔彦之〕張〔鵬〕
翰江〔東〕高〔世彦〕都指揮僉事
胡〔永錫〕湯〔卿〕王〔三錫〕各事事
於外如期乃合提學副使陳
punctuated: 先二月至永懐，時屆允㲉，勤用休于資。迺若總理河道右副都御史郭〔持平〕，撫陽右僉都御史戴〔時宗〕，監祭御史巡鹽〔舒遷〕、党〔承賜〕，印馬黎〔循典〕，咸賛厥成。右布查〔應兆〕，左叅政胡〔體乾〕，政王〔慎中〕、劉〔友仁〕，左叅良〔傅〕，右叅議左〔傑〕、王〔傅〕、王〔家〕、湯〔紹恩〕、端〔廷赦〕、張〔素〕，僉事張〔晃〕、林〔雲同〕、趙〔彦之〕、張〔鵬〕、翰、江〔東〕、高〔世彦〕，都指揮僉事胡〔永錫〕、湯〔卿〕、王〔三錫〕，各事事於外，如期乃合。提學副使陳
translation_en:
…two months earlier, [he] arrived at Yonghuai [?]. When the time came, [the wording concerning diligence and resources is unclear: 時屆允㲉，勤用休于資]. As for Guo Chiping, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief administering the waterways; Dai Shizong, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, with a supervisory responsibility described as 撫陽 [?]; Shu Qian and Dang Chengci, associated here with censorial duties and salt inspection [the titles and their allocation are garbled]; and Li Xundian, associated with horse administration [?]: all assisted in bringing the undertaking to completion.
Zha Yingzhao held the post abbreviated here as “Right Administrative Commissioner” [?]. Hu Tiqian was Left Administration Vice Commissioner. Wang Shenzhong and Liu Youren appear under the incomplete title 政 [?], and Liang Fu under the incomplete title 左叅 [?]. Zuo Jie, Wang Fu, Wang Jia, Tang Shaoen, Duan Tingshe, and Zhang Su were Right Administration Assistant Commissioners. Zhang Huang, Lin Yuntong, Zhao Yanzhi, Zhang Peng, Han [?], Jiang Dong, and Gao Shiyan were Surveillance Commissioners. Hu Yongxi, Tang Qing, and Wang Sanxi were Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. Each attended to his duties outside, and they then assembled at the appointed time. Education Intendant Chen …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
東
所選士二千二百有竒凡
三試之得士八十人號名梓
文以
獻
興孰非由上之所作哉盖覲
於此方人士之盛而知
今河南所履之域則商
===
墟與周之新邑在焉方殷之
末民化於紂毫相千里之
皆爲頑民武王以羣后之師
濟于孟津爲牧野之陳會旦
而商郊清明其後嘗衰矣宣
王中起則自濟之洛狩于圃
田以至敖山而朝諸侯故周
punctuated:
東所選士二千二百有竒，凡三試之，得士八十人，號名梓文以獻。
興孰非由上之所作哉？盖覲於此方人士之盛而知。
今河南所履之域，則商墟與周之新邑在焉。方殷之末，民化於紂，毫相千里之皆爲頑民。武王以羣后之師濟于孟津，爲牧野之陳，會旦而商郊清明。其後嘗衰矣，宣王中起，則自濟之洛，狩于圃田，以至敖山而朝諸侯。故周
translation_en:
…Dong had selected more than 2,200 candidates. They were examined in three sessions, and eighty were selected. Their names were announced and their compositions printed for presentation.
What flourishing does not arise from the initiative of the ruler above? This can be understood by observing [?] the abundance of talented scholars in this region.
Within the territory now encompassed by Henan lie the ruins of Shang and the new city of Zhou. At the end of the Yin dynasty, the people were transformed by Zhou, its last ruler; throughout the thousand-li region of Bo and Xiang [?], all became recalcitrant people. King Wu led the armies of the assembled lords across the river at Mengjin and arrayed them at Muye. By daybreak, the outskirts of Shang were cleared and peace restored. Later, Zhou underwent decline. King Xuan arose to revive it: he went from the Ji River to the Luo River, hunted at Putian, and proceeded as far as Mount Ao, where he received the feudal lords in audience. Thus, Zhou…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
之盛時人才衆多詩人歌之
藹藹王多吉人生甫及申維
周之翰之詩列之於雅以著
中興得人之功雖其仁澤之
厚道化之深積漸所致然君
子所過固有以化人者禮
脩於戎甲之中聲明動於東
===
服之表宜其昏者以明棄者
以起而成有周之隆也舞
宋季豫州久汙於胡不見王
者之物已數百年惟我
高皇帝以神武啓運再造區宇當
其時
大輅親臨徯后之民遽覩
punctuated:
之盛時，人才衆多，詩人歌之：「藹藹，王多吉人。」「生甫及申，維周之翰。」之詩列之於雅，以著中興得人之功。雖其仁澤之厚、道化之深，積漸所致，然君子所過，固有以化人者。禮脩於戎甲之中，聲明動於東服之表，宜其昏者以明，棄者以起，而成有周之隆也。
舞宋季，豫州久汙於胡，不見王者之物已數百年。惟我高皇帝以神武啓運，再造區宇。當其時，大輅親臨，徯后之民遽覩
translation_en:
…during Zhou’s flourishing, talented men were numerous. The poets celebrated them: “In abundant numbers, the king has many worthy men”; “He brought forth Fu and Shen, the supporting pillars of Zhou.” These poems were included among the Odes of the Book of Poetry to make manifest the achievement of securing worthy men for the restoration. Although the generosity of benevolent beneficence and the depth of moral transformation resulted from gradual accumulation, wherever the noble man passed, he assuredly possessed the means to transform others. Ritual propriety was cultivated amid arms and armor, and the renown of enlightened rule stirred even the lands beyond the eastern domains. It was fitting that the benighted should thereby become enlightened and the neglected should rise, bringing about the greatness of Zhou.
[?] In the closing years of the Song, Yuzhou had long been defiled by the Hu and had not seen the trappings of a true king for several hundred years. Our Emperor Gao alone inaugurated a new dynastic destiny through his divine martial prowess and reconstituted the realm. At that time, when his grand imperial carriage arrived in person, the people who had awaited their sovereign suddenly beheld …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人之作歡忻鼓舞如蟄斯震涵
昏鄙偕之俗其去也忽焉躋
習於仁義發形於禮樂以而
副上之求堪世之用者宜其
衆也今
天子建中下民以道術陶成一
德意感孚罔已不大聲色而儀刑
===
徧於四方須者
孝思永念展謁
寢園輿從所由佚及皆出豫州之
境四海黎庶引領舉踵欲見
無從而車馬之音羽旄之美
中州之人獨得於見聞昔東
都之狩人覩其堅好之卓謂
punctuated: 聖人之作，歡忻鼓舞，如蟄斯震。涵昏鄙偕之俗，其去也忽焉；躋習於仁義，發形於禮樂，以而副上之求、堪世之用者，宜其衆也。今，天子建中下民，以道術陶成一德，意感孚罔已，不大聲色，而儀刑徧於四方。須者，孝思永念，展謁寢園，輿從所由，佚及皆出豫州之境。四海黎庶，引領舉踵，欲見無從，而車馬之音、羽旄之美，中州之人獨得於見聞。昔東都之狩，人覩其堅好之卓，謂
translation_en:
…the arising of the sage. They rejoiced and danced with delight, like hibernating creatures stirred by thunder. Their ingrained customs of ignorance and vulgarity [?] were suddenly cast off. They advanced in the practice of benevolence and righteousness, expressing these through ritual and music; it was fitting that many should thus meet the sovereign’s demands and prove useful to the age.

Now the Son of Heaven establishes the mean among the people below, molding them through the Way and its teachings into a common virtue. His intentions inspire trust without cease; without raising his voice or assuming a stern countenance, his exemplary conduct reaches throughout the realm. Recently [?], ever mindful in his filial devotion, he paid his respects at the imperial tombs. The route taken by his carriage and retinue, and the benefits extending from it [?], all passed through the territory of Yuzhou. The common people throughout the empire craned their necks and stood on tiptoe, longing to see him but having no opportunity. The people of Zhongzhou alone were able to hear the sounds of his carriages and horses and behold the beauty of his feathered and yak-tail banners. Formerly, during the royal hunt at the eastern capital, people saw their outstanding sturdiness and beauty [?], and said of …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
齊之馬嗟歎而頌之曰是夫
成之君子不可名言其德惟
其有聞而已也是知
聖君之旂色鸞聲昭回噦噦皆所
以改新中州之耳目而聳其
震曜之氣誘其濯磨之心
濟多士之生有不思奮其宜
===
同於愷天子之頌哉凡天
子之行無非事者隊詩內
合端甯量養老助農以觀好
惡出誅賞其大者乃在於數
奏明揚故甫草之役所以
徒記所謂射而取士者是也
今論選之典適應其期必有
punctuated: 齊之馬，嗟歎而頌之曰：「是夫成之君子，不可名言其德，惟其有聞而已也。」是知聖君之旂色鸞聲，昭回噦噦，皆所以改新中州之耳目，而聳其震曜之氣，誘其濯磨之心。濟多士之生，有不思奮其宜，同於愷天子之頌哉？凡天子之行，無非事者。隊詩內合端甯量，養老助農，以觀好惡，出誅賞。其大者乃在於數奏明揚。故甫草之役，所以徒記所謂「射而取士」者是也。今論選之典，適應其期，必有
translation_en:
…the horses of Qi [?], and, sighing in admiration, praised him, saying: “This accomplished gentleman [?]—his virtue cannot be named or expressed; one can only hear of it.” Thus we know that the sage sovereign’s brilliant banners and jingling carriage bells, shining and sounding in harmony, all serve to renew what the people of Zhongzhou see and hear, to rouse their splendid spirit, and to inspire their resolve to cleanse and polish themselves. Among the many scholars [?], could any fail to think of exerting themselves as they ought, joining in praise of the gracious Son of Heaven?
Whenever the Son of Heaven travels, there is always business to attend to. [The passage 隊詩內合端甯量 is unclear.] He provides for the aged and assists farming, observes what people love and hate, and dispenses punishments and rewards. His greater purpose lies in repeatedly receiving recommendations and publicly advancing worthy men [?]. Thus the expedition to the hunting grounds of Fu exemplifies what the record [?] calls “selecting scholars through archery.” Now the ceremony of evaluating and selecting men happens to coincide with this occasion; surely there will be…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
異材孕嶽而降如詩人所稱
爲申爲甫者以鳴中興之盛
則諸士之進固關於王氣
大政以明
聖君之行之有事非獨爲三歲而
比之常典已也夫豈賢材之
句於上之所作及其成也則
===
聖君之行之有事非獨爲三歲而
上之治常因以明而其名聲
因以行此烝民崧高之所
爲宣王之美也夫士能興於
聖人之化以自成其材又以
其材見於用而名於世以
頌
聖君脩道致治之美者於此乎徵
punctuated: 異材孕嶽而降，如詩人所稱爲申爲甫者，以鳴中興之盛。則諸士之進，固關於王氣大政，以明聖君之行之有事，非獨爲三歲而比之常典已也。夫豈賢材之句於上之所作，及其成也，則聖君之行之有事，非獨爲三歲而上之治常因以明，而其名聲因以行。此《烝民》《崧高》之所爲宣王之美也。夫士能興於聖人之化，以自成其材，又以其材見於用而名於世，以頌聖君脩道致治之美者，於此乎徵
translation_en: …exceptional talents, nurtured by the sacred mountains and sent down, like those whom the poet called Shen and Fu, to proclaim the splendor of a restoration. The advancement of these scholars is thus indeed bound up with royal vitality and great affairs of government [?], making manifest that the sage ruler’s actions have a purpose; it is not merely the regular institution of comparing candidates once every three years. How could worthy talent be constrained [?] by what the ruler undertakes? When it reaches fulfillment, then the sage ruler’s actions have a purpose, not merely for three years [the transcription repeats an earlier passage here, leaving the syntax doubtful]; the ruler’s governance is thereby continually made illustrious, and his renown spreads accordingly. This is how the poems “The Multitude of the People” (Zheng min) and “Lofty Mountains” (Song gao) praise King Xuan. Scholars can be inspired by the sage’s transforming influence to develop their own talents, then have those talents employed and become renowned in the world, thereby celebrating the sage ruler’s excellence in cultivating the Way and bringing about good government. Evidence of this is to be found here…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
而〔恒〕也實始進之豈不與有
幸與
江西袁州府儒學教授以
□序
punctuated:
而〔恒〕也實始進之，豈不與有幸與？

江西袁州府儒學教授以□序。
translation_en:
…and I, Heng, was indeed the first to advance them. Could I not also count myself fortunate?

Preface by Yi □ [?], Instructor in the Confucian School of Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

嘉靖十九年河南鄉試

監臨官：巡按河南監察御史陳蕙〔邦瞻，福建，己丑進士〕。

提調官：河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使范鏓〔平甫，江西樂平縣籍，遼東瀋陽中衛人，丁丑進士〕。河南等處承宣布政使司左參議周相〔大鄉，浙江鄞縣人，癸未進士〕。

監試官：河南等處提刑按察司按察使龍奇〔道亨，湖廣茶陵，丁丑進士〕。河南等處提刑按察司副使張乘恩〔君□□，直隸□州，辛□進士〕。

考試官：江西袁州府儒學教授趙恒〔志貞，福建晉江縣，戊戌進士〕。江西饒州府樂平縣儒學教諭王珂〔仲輝，□□，戊□□〕。

同考試官：直隸真定府深州儒學學正孫勳〔建卿，廣東南海縣人，甲午貢士〕。直隸廬州府無爲州巢縣儒學教諭鄭冢〔秉憲，□□，己卯□〕。湖廣永州府道州江華縣儒學教諭李濬〔原德，□□□□□，丁□貢士〕。浙江台州府寧海縣儒學教諭陳席珍〔□□，福建□官縣人，戊子貢士〕。山西沁州武鄉縣儒學教諭雍焯〔□仲，陝西□□□人，丁酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Henan Provincial Examination, the nineteenth year of Jiajing (1540)

Supervising Official
Chen Hui, Investigating Censor touring Henan. His courtesy name was Bangzhan; he was from Fujian and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jichou year.

Proctors
Fan Cong, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Pingfu; his registered domicile was Leping County, Jiangxi, and he was a native of Shenyang Central Guard, Liaodong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Zhou Xiang, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Daxiang; he was from Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Examination Inspectors
Long Qi, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he was from Chaling, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Zhang Cheng'en, Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name began with Jun [remainder illegible]; he was from an illegibly named subprefecture in Zhili and was a metropolitan graduate of a year beginning with xin [remainder illegible].

Examiners
Zhao Heng, Prefectural School Instructor of Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Zhizhen; he was from Jinjiang County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Wang Ke, County School Instructor of Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Zhonghui; his place of origin is illegible, and the remaining annotation reads only “wu…” [?].

Associate Examiners
Sun Xun, Subprefectural School Instructor of Shenzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Jianqing; he was from Nanhai County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jiawu year.
Zheng Zhong [?], County School Instructor of Chao County, Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Bingxian; his place of origin is illegible. The annotation gives the jimao year, followed by an illegible character [?].
Li Jun, County School Instructor of Jianghua County, Daozhou Subprefecture, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Yuande; his place of origin is illegible. He was a tribute student of a year beginning with ding [remainder illegible].
Chen Xizhen, County School Instructor of Ninghai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name is illegible; he was from a county transcribed as “□guan” in Fujian [?] and was a tribute student of the wuzi year.
Yong Zhuo, County School Instructor of Wuxiang County, Qinzhou Subprefecture, Shanxi. His courtesy name ended in Zhong [first character illegible]; he was from an illegible locality in Shaanxi and was a tribute student of the dingyou year.

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
克己復禮爲仁一日克己復禮天下歸仁
焉爲仁由己而由人乎哉
脩身以道脩道以仁
見其禮而知其政聞其樂而知其德由百
世之後等百世之王莫之能違也自生
民以來未有夫子也
易
臨剛浸而長說而順剛中而應大亨以正
天之道也
===
九五甘節吉往有尚
夫易何爲者也夫易開物成務冒天下之
道如斯而已者也是故聖人以通天下
之志以定天下之業以斷天下之疑
是故易者象也象也者像也
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

克己復禮爲仁。一日克己復禮，天下歸仁焉。爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？

脩身以道，脩道以仁。

見其禮而知其政，聞其樂而知其德。由百世之後，等百世之王，莫之能違也。自生民以來，未有夫子也。

易

臨，剛浸而長，說而順，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之道也。

九五，甘節，吉，往有尚。

夫易何爲者也？夫易，開物成務，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。是故聖人以通天下之志，以定天下之業，以斷天下之疑。

是故易者，象也；象也者，像也。

書

帝曰：「咨！四岳，有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」帝
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

To restrain oneself and return to ritual propriety is benevolence. Once one restrains oneself and returns to ritual propriety, all under Heaven will acknowledge one's benevolence. Practicing benevolence depends on oneself; could it depend on others?

Cultivate oneself through the Way, and cultivate the Way through benevolence.

Seeing his rites, one knows his government; hearing his music, one knows his virtue. Even from a hundred generations later, one can appraise the kings of a hundred generations, and none can depart from this standard. Since humankind first came into being, there has never been anyone like the Master.

Book of Changes

In Lin (Approach), the firm gradually increases and grows. Joyous and yielding, with the firm occupying the central position and receiving a response, it brings great success through correctness: this is the Way of Heaven.

Nine in the fifth place: sweet restraint. Auspicious. To go forward brings esteem.

What does the Book of Changes do? The Book of Changes discloses things, brings undertakings to completion, and encompasses the ways of all under Heaven. That is all. Therefore, the sages use it to comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven, to settle the undertakings of all under Heaven, and to resolve the doubts of all under Heaven.

Thus, the Changes consists of images; images are likenesses.

Book of Documents

The emperor said: “Ah, Four Mountains, is there anyone who can oversee my three rites?” All replied: “Bo Yi.” The emperor …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟
清伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
若作酒醴爾惟麴糵若作和羹爾惟鹽梅
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日歲月日時
無易百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家用
平康
惟文王尚克脩和我有夏亦惟有若虢叔
有若閎夭有若散宜生有若泰顛有若
南宮括
===
詩
南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履成之
我覯之子維其有章矣維其有章矣是以
有慶矣
成王之孚下土之式永言孝思孝思維則
王釐爾成來咨來茹嗟嗟保介維莫之春
亦又何求如何新畬於皇來牟將受厥
明明昭上帝迄用康年命我衆人庤乃
錢鎛奄觀銍艾
punctuated:
曰：「俞！咨，伯！汝作秩宗，夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞！往，欽哉！」

若作酒醴，爾惟麴糵；若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。

王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。歲月日時無易，百穀用成，乂用明，俊民用章，家用平康。

惟文王尚克脩和我有夏，亦惟有若虢叔，有若閎夭，有若散宜生，有若泰顛，有若南宮括。

詩

南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。

我覯之子，維其有章矣！維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。

成王之孚，下土之式。永言孝思，孝思維則。

王釐爾成，來咨來茹。嗟嗟保介，維莫之春，亦又何求？如何新畬？於皇來牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。命我衆人，庤乃錢鎛，奄觀銍艾。
translation_en:
…said: “Yes! Ah, Bo! You shall serve as Director of Ancestral Sacrifices. Be reverent morning and night; be upright and pure.” Bo bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui and Long. The emperor said: “Yes! Go, and discharge your duties reverently!”

If wine or sweet liquor is to be made, you are its yeast and malt; if a well-seasoned broth is to be made, you are its salt and sour plums.

The king examines the year, the high ministers the month, and the various officials the day. When years, months, and days follow their proper seasons without disruption, the grains ripen, government is enlightened, worthy men gain recognition, and households enjoy peace and well-being.

King Wen was indeed able to cultivate harmony throughout our land of Xia, also because he had men such as Guo Shu, Hong Yao, San Yisheng, Tai Dian, and Nangong Kuo.

Book of Odes

In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines entwine them. Joyful is the noble gentleman; blessings bring him fulfillment.

I behold that gentleman: how distinguished he is! Because he is so distinguished, blessings attend him.

King Cheng’s trustworthiness was a model for the lands below. Ever cherish filial thoughts; filial thoughts are the guiding rule.

The king has bestowed established rules upon you; come to consult, come to deliberate. Ah, you agricultural assistants! It is now late spring: what further things must you seek? How fare the fields in their second and third years of cultivation? Ah, splendid are the wheat and barley, soon to attain their ripeness. May the bright and glorious Lord on High finally grant us a bountiful year. Command our people to prepare their spades and hoes; soon we shall see the reaping with sickles.

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
春秋
三月公會鄭伯于垂　鄭伯以璧假許田
夏四月丁未公及鄭伯盟于越〔桓公元年俱〕
秋公子友如陳〔莊公二十有七年〕
冬晉趙穿帥師侵崇〔宣公元年〕　秦師伐
晉〔宣公二年〕
春王正月晉人滅赤狄甲氏及留吁〔宣公十有六年〕
夏晉伐鮮虞〔昭公十有二年〕
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
===
禮記
明七教以興民德
故學之為父子焉學之為君臣焉學之為
長幼焉父子君臣長幼之道得而國治
德者性之端也樂者德之華也金石絲竹
樂之器也詩言其志也歌詠其聲也舞
動其容也三者本於心然後樂器從之
是故情深而文明氣盛而化神和順積
punctuated:
春秋
三月，公會鄭伯于垂。鄭伯以璧假許田。夏四月丁未，公及鄭伯盟于越。〔桓公元年俱〕
秋，公子友如陳。〔莊公二十有七年〕
冬，晉趙穿帥師侵崇。〔宣公元年〕秦師伐晉。〔宣公二年〕
春，王正月，晉人滅赤狄甲氏及留吁。〔宣公十有六年〕
夏，晉伐鮮虞。〔昭公十有二年〕
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞。〔昭公十有五年〕

禮記
明七教以興民德。
故學之為父子焉，學之為君臣焉，學之為長幼焉。父子、君臣、長幼之道得，而國治。
德者，性之端也；樂者，德之華也；金石絲竹，樂之器也。詩，言其志也；歌，詠其聲也；舞，動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。是故情深而文明，氣盛而化神，和順積
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals
In the third month, the Duke met the Earl of Zheng at Chui. The Earl of Zheng used a jade disk to borrow the fields of Xu. In summer, on the dingwei day of the fourth month, the Duke and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Yue. 〔All the preceding entries are from the first year of Duke Huan.〕
In autumn, the ducal son You went to Chen. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang.〕
In winter, Zhao Chuan of Jin led an army to invade Chong. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 An army of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Second year of Duke Xuan.〕
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the men of Jin destroyed the Jia and Liuxu peoples of the Red Di. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
In summer, Jin attacked Xianyu. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Zhao.〕
Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites
Make the seven teachings clear in order to cultivate the people's virtue.
Thus they are taught how to act as fathers and sons, as rulers and ministers, and as elders and juniors. When the proper ways governing fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, and elders and juniors are realized, the state is well governed.
Virtue is the proper expression of human nature; music is the flowering of virtue. Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are the instruments of music. Poetry expresses one's aspirations; song gives them voice in sustained sound; dance expresses them through bodily movement. These three are rooted in the heart, and only afterward do musical instruments accompany them. Thus, when feeling is deep, its outward expression is luminous; when vital energy is abundant, its transforming power is wondrous; harmony and accord accumulate…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
中而英華發外惟樂不可以爲僞
射鄉之禮所以仁鄉黨也食饗之禮所以
仁賓客也
第貳場
論〔一道〕
吾道一以貫之
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉各一人詔〔元光元年〕

〔開元四年〕

translation_en:
…within, and its brilliance manifests itself outwardly. Music alone cannot be feigned. The archery and village ceremonies serve to show benevolence toward the people of the local community; the ceremonies of feeding and feasting serve to show benevolence toward guests.

Second Session

Discourse 〔One topic〕
“My Way is threaded together by a single principle.”

Edicts, Pronouncements, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose, in the manner of the Han dynasty, an edict ordering each commandery and kingdom to recommend one person distinguished for filial devotion and integrity. 〔First year of Yuanguang〕
Compose, in the manner of the Tang dynasty, a document appointing Song Jing and Su Ting, Ministers of Personnel, as Joint Managers of Affairs of the Secretariat–Chancellery.
Compose, in the manner of the Song dynasty, a memorial of thanks for the appointment of Li Zhi, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, as Vice Minister of Personnel, and of Li Hang to serve concurrently as Adviser to the Heir Apparent [?]. 〔First year of Zhidao〕
〔Fourth year of Kaiyuan: apparently a displaced annotation to the Tang topic above.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Leaving an official post or assigned service without authorization.
Concealment to evade labor service.
Prohibiting ceremonial welcomes and send-offs.
Failing to meet the deadline for joining a military expedition.
Recusal when hearing litigation.

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
第叄塲
策五道
問宋儒言帝王之學與韋布不同章句之
業與經綸異夫古者人生十五年則自
天子之元子衆子下逮士庶人俊秀皆
入大學不知古天子與庶人之學其亦
有同乎否宋儒之所謂學者其於古者
大小學之教又可如也夫人君以務學
為急而學以正心為要固矣然又欲人
主讀經史則以尚書唐史為先者其亦
可互相發明與且二書之尤為急者其
於帝王之心學何如也肆我
===
列聖繼作於聖學興理至于
東宮授受又獨明備誠以天下之命所係而
諭教不可不先者也我
太祖高皇帝嘗采經傳格言為
儲君昭鑑錄以訓戒
太子我
punctuated:
第叄塲

策五道

問：宋儒言：「帝王之學與韋布不同，章句之業與經綸異。」夫古者，人生十五年，則自天子之元子、衆子，下逮士庶人俊秀，皆入大學。不知古天子與庶人之學，其亦有同乎否？宋儒之所謂學者，其於古者大小學之教，又可如也？夫人君以務學為急，而學以正心為要，固矣。然又欲人主讀經史，則以尚書、唐史為先者，其亦可互相發明與？且二書之尤為急者，其於帝王之心學何如也？肆我列聖繼作，於聖學興理，至于東宮授受，又獨明備，誠以天下之命所係，而諭教不可不先者也。我太祖高皇帝嘗采經傳格言，為《儲君昭鑑錄》，以訓戒太子。我
translation_en:
Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: A Song Confucian said: “The learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoners in plain cloth; the study of textual divisions and phrases differs from ordering the affairs of the realm.” In antiquity, when boys reached fifteen years of age, all entered the Great Learning, from the Son of Heaven’s eldest son and other sons down to the outstanding sons of officers and commoners. Was there, then, anything shared by the learning of the Son of Heaven and that of commoners in antiquity? How did what the Song Confucians called learning relate to the instruction of the ancient Elementary Learning and Great Learning [?]?

It is certainly true that a ruler must make learning an urgent concern, and that the essential purpose of learning is to rectify the mind. Yet there was also the recommendation that, when a ruler reads the classics and histories, he should begin with the Book of Documents and the History of the Tang. Can these teachings illuminate one another? And how does the particular urgency accorded these two books relate to the learning of the mind practiced by emperors and kings?

Our successive sage emperors have thus arisen one after another, promoting the learning of the sages and principle [?]. In the transmission and reception of instruction in the Eastern Palace, the residence of the heir apparent, their provisions have been especially clear and comprehensive. This is truly because the fate of the realm depends upon him, and his instruction must therefore take precedence. Our Emperor Taizu Gao once selected exemplary sayings from the classics and their commentaries to compile the Record of Illuminating Mirrors for the Heir Apparent (Chujun zhaojian lu), with which to instruct and admonish the crown prince. Our…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
祖文皇帝則又采聖賢之言爲
聖學心法一書綱目具舉則知宋臣之言良不
爲誣而我
二聖之徽指大義質諸大學而無疑者此亦可
贊揚其萬一與我
皇上敬一有箴五箴有註獨契道體於千百載
之上雖非專爲
東宮爲之而所言莫非正心脩身之道固
二聖心法之傳也不知今日在
宮寮所以輔成勸相者亦可以不外于茲也
其敬識之
===
問人之言曰爲君難爲臣不易君之大者
曰允總臣之大者曰履盛滿至於保泰
一事君臣共之遭際不預馬從古君臣
知而善處之者誰與慶曆元祐之間盛
矣擬之太甲成王或未及也其中登用
之臣若范文正公司馬溫公俱一代偉
人仁哲二宗之信任初亦甚篤矣此皆盛
punctuated:
祖文皇帝則又采聖賢之言，爲《聖學心法》一書，綱目具舉，則知宋臣之言良不爲誣。而我二聖之徽指大義，質諸《大學》而無疑者，此亦可贊揚其萬一與？我皇上敬一有箴，五箴有註，獨契道體於千百載之上。雖非專爲東宮爲之，而所言莫非正心脩身之道，固二聖心法之傳也。不知今日在宮寮所以輔成勸相者，亦可以不外于茲也？其敬識之。

問：人之言曰：「爲君難，爲臣不易。」君之大者曰允總，臣之大者曰履盛滿。至於保泰一事，君臣共之，遭際不預馬？從古君臣知而善處之者誰與？慶曆、元祐之間盛矣，擬之太甲、成王，或未及也。其中登用之臣，若范文正公、司馬溫公，俱一代偉人。仁、哲二宗之信任，初亦甚篤矣。此皆盛
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen, the ancestral emperor, further gathered the words of sages and worthies into a book, Essential Teachings of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), setting out both its main principles and its particulars. Thus we know that the words of the Song minister were indeed no misrepresentation. The lofty purport and great principles of our two sage emperors admit of no doubt when tested against the Great Learning. Might you offer even a small measure of praise and exposition of them?

Our reigning emperor composed an Admonition on Reverence for Unity and supplied annotations to the Five Admonitions, uniquely apprehending the substance of the Way as transmitted from a thousand and more years ago. Although these were not composed exclusively for the heir apparent, everything they say concerns rectifying the mind and cultivating the self. They assuredly transmit the essential teachings of our two sage emperors. Might the means by which officials of the heir apparent’s household today assist his development, encourage him, and guide him likewise remain within these teachings? Set this down reverently.

Question: It has been said, “To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy.” The ruler’s great task is to exercise overall direction with impartiality [?]; the minister’s great task is to conduct himself amid flourishing prosperity. As for preserving peace and prosperity, ruler and ministers share this responsibility. Does it not depend upon the circumstances they encounter [?]? Among rulers and ministers since antiquity, who understood this and handled it well?

The Qingli and Yuanyou eras were flourishing times; compared with them, even the reigns of Tai Jia and King Cheng perhaps fell short. Among the ministers appointed then, Duke Fan Wenzheng and Duke Sima of Wen were both outstanding men of their age. The emperors Renzong and Zhezong initially placed very deep trust in them. These were all flourishing…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
朝未久身就退閒用不及究業無光顯
豈盡遭際之難耶抑二公當時舉動亦
間有失其失之最大者何事可得聞與
時固有議之者果定論與二公亦志
伊尹之志學周公之學者何卒不能致
其君爲太甲成王而保持豐亨豫大之
業其故何與使諸士子身親其事果將
何以慮始何以慮終格正爕和之道必
有說也願詳著于篇以觀經濟之學
===
問讀史非徒以其文也可以辯王伯盛衰之
節謹邪正審義利觀忠孝明出處者也
試舉平日所疑者言之于泓之戰不鼓
不成列中年之後擊金而退均之爲仁
也而成敗何以異登牀一盟竟以救宋
救陳一退遂以安民均之爲義也而心
術何以分是王伯之當辯也以大將軍
之貴而爲之揖客其所執者何禮稱天
下之平而爲人結轔其所示者何意是
punctuated:
朝，未久身就退閒，用不及究，業無光顯，豈盡遭際之難耶？抑二公當時舉動亦間有失？其失之最大者何事，可得聞與？時固有議之者，果定論與？二公亦志伊尹之志，學周公之學者，何卒不能致其君爲太甲、成王，而保持豐亨豫大之業？其故何與？使諸士子身親其事，果將何以慮始，何以慮終？格正爕和之道，必有說也。願詳著于篇，以觀經濟之學。

問：讀史非徒以其文也，可以辯王伯盛衰之節，謹邪正，審義利，觀忠孝，明出處者也。試舉平日所疑者言之：于泓之戰，不鼓不成列；中年之後，擊金而退。均之爲仁也，而成敗何以異？登牀一盟，竟以救宋；救陳一退，遂以安民。均之爲義也，而心術何以分？是王伯之當辯也。以大將軍之貴，而爲之揖客，其所執者何禮？稱天下之平，而爲人結轔，其所示者何意？是
translation_en:
…court, yet before long they withdrew into retirement. Their service could not be carried through, and their achievements attained no brilliance. Was this entirely due to the difficulty of their circumstances? Or were there also occasional errors in the two gentlemen’s conduct at the time? What were their greatest errors? May we hear of them? There were certainly people who criticized them then, but were those judgments conclusive? These two gentlemen also embraced Yi Yin’s aspirations and studied the Duke of Zhou’s learning. Why, in the end, could they not make their sovereigns into a Tai Jia or a King Cheng and preserve an enterprise of abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness? What explains this? If you candidates had personally faced these affairs, how would you have considered their beginnings, and how their outcomes? You must have something to say about the way to rectify the ruler and bring affairs into harmony. Set it out fully in your essays, so that we may assess your learning in statecraft.

Question: Reading history is not merely a matter of appreciating its writing. Through it one can distinguish kingship from hegemony and discern the critical points of flourishing and decline; attend carefully to the distinction between depravity and uprightness; examine righteousness and profit; observe loyalty and filial devotion; and understand when to enter office and when to withdraw. Let us raise some longstanding doubts for discussion. At the battle of Hong, the drums were not sounded against an enemy whose ranks had not yet formed; after middle age [?], metal instruments were struck to signal withdrawal. Both were acts of benevolence: why, then, did their outcomes differ in success and failure? A single covenant made by mounting a couch [?] ultimately saved Song; a single withdrawal when rescuing Chen brought peace to the people. Both were acts of righteousness: how, then, are the intentions behind them to be distinguished? These are matters in which kingship and hegemony must be distinguished. Despite the exalted rank of General-in-Chief, someone was treated as a guest greeted with a bow: what ritual propriety was being upheld? Praised as an impartial judge of all under Heaven, someone nevertheless joined carriage wheels for another [?]: what intention did this display? These are…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
氣節之當立也投巫于河止殉于葬其
術同也不知何者爲仁立公孫洩存伍
員祠其見同也不知何者爲正是邪正
之當謹也左袒以安社稷勃之忠也而
亦有謀傾諸呂者不知何者之功爲大
殺佞以復父讎琇之孝也而亦有請代
父死者不知何者之行爲優是忠孝之
當觀也魯儒之歸陳步愚則甚矣而兩
生尚在何以長往四老之避秦政行則
===
清矣而太子一迎何以遽至是出處之
當明也不受贓錢之賕介矣較之見幾
去官而受賜黄金者孰誠邪請□□□
之大義矣較之上麥濟軍而不領馮翊
者孰正邪是義利之當審也此皆有疑
於史而未定者諸士子習之久矣其折
衷之論去取之意幸詳以告我
問先儒程子有云國祚之所以祈天永命
常人之至於聖賢皆工夫到處以有此
punctuated:
氣節之當立也。投巫于河，止殉于葬，其術同也，不知何者爲仁；立公孫洩，存伍員祠，其見同也，不知何者爲正。是邪正之當謹也。左袒以安社稷，勃之忠也，而亦有謀傾諸呂者，不知何者之功爲大；殺佞以復父讎，琇之孝也，而亦有請代父死者，不知何者之行爲優。是忠孝之當觀也。魯儒之歸陳步，愚則甚矣，而兩生尚在，何以長往？四老之避秦政，行則清矣，而太子一迎，何以遽至？是出處之當明也。不受贓錢之賕，介矣，較之見幾去官而受賜黄金者，孰誠邪？請□□□之大義矣，較之上麥濟軍而不領馮翊者，孰正邪？是義利之當審也。此皆有疑於史而未定者。諸士子習之久矣，其折衷之論、去取之意，幸詳以告我。
問：先儒程子有云：「國祚之所以祈天永命，常人之至於聖賢，皆工夫到處以有此
translation_en:
…moral integrity must be established. Casting a shaman into the river and putting a stop to human sacrifice at burials were alike in their methods; I do not know which was benevolent. Establishing Gongsun Xie [?] and preserving the shrine of Wu Yun were alike in their outlook; I do not know which was right. Thus one must take care in distinguishing wrong from right. Baring his left arm to secure the altars of soil and grain displayed Bo’s loyalty; yet there was also someone who devised the overthrow of the Lü clan. I do not know whose achievement was greater. Killing a treacherous man to avenge his father displayed Xiu’s filial devotion; yet there was also someone who asked to die in his father’s place. I do not know whose conduct was superior. Thus loyalty and filial devotion must be examined. The Confucian scholars of Lu who went over to Chen Bu [?] were exceedingly foolish; yet the two scholars were still there—why did they withdraw for good? The conduct of the Four Elders in avoiding Qin rule was pure; yet why did they come so promptly as soon as the heir apparent invited them? Thus taking office and withdrawing must be clearly understood. Refusing a bribe of illicit money showed integrity; compared with someone who perceived the first signs of trouble, left office, and accepted a gift of gold, who was sincere? Requesting … was an act of great righteousness [?]; compared with someone who presented wheat to supply the army but declined appointment as Governor of Fengyi, who was upright? Thus righteousness and profit must be carefully distinguished. These are all unresolved doubts concerning the historical record. You examination candidates have studied these matters for a long time. Please explain to me in detail your considered judgments and your reasons for accepting or rejecting these courses of action.
Question: The earlier Confucian Master Cheng once said: “A dynasty’s success in praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate, and an ordinary person’s attainment of sagehood or worthiness, both come about when sustained effort reaches the point of producing this…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
應夫祈天永命如三代有道之長尚矣
下此如馬上藉一劒之任者惡聞儒書
之說晉陽并臣虜之耻者遂失義兵之
正陳橋倒戈大綱掃地皆能光有天下
祚延數百豈必皆有道以致之與由臨
淄而入靖宮闈之亂者自不免於奢縱
之風乘夷難而起承炎宋之統者亦不
脫乎俗儒之習而皆撥亂爲治身致中
興又何故與學而至於聖賢如道統□
===
諸人尚矣下此如治天人之學者或□
於陰陽之秘著原道之篇者或遺夫格
致之功入仕胡元未免失身彼皆爲時
名儒尊崇聖學豈其於道有未聞與繼
僞學之後而願爲朱子忠臣者尚未明
於存心致知之辯值靖康之際而獨得
程氏真傳者亦未見於出處去就之機
而皆講學爲功道賴不墜又何故與抑
別有可取與夫國統正於上道統明於
punctuated: 應。夫祈天永命，如三代有道之長，尚矣。下此，如馬上藉一劒之任者，惡聞儒書之說；晉陽并臣虜之耻者，遂失義兵之正；陳橋倒戈，大綱掃地，皆能光有天下，祚延數百，豈必皆有道以致之與？由臨淄而入，靖宮闈之亂者，自不免於奢縱之風；乘夷難而起，承炎宋之統者，亦不脫乎俗儒之習，而皆撥亂爲治，身致中興，又何故與？學而至於聖賢，如道統□諸人，尚矣。下此，如治天人之學者，或□於陰陽之秘；著原道之篇者，或遺夫格致之功；入仕胡元，未免失身，彼皆爲時名儒，尊崇聖學，豈其於道有未聞與？繼僞學之後，而願爲朱子忠臣者，尚未明於存心致知之辯；值靖康之際，而獨得程氏真傳者，亦未見於出處去就之機，而皆講學爲功，道賴不墜，又何故與？抑別有可取與？夫國統正於上，道統明於
translation_en:
…response. As for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate, the long reigns of the Three Dynasties, which possessed the Way, stand as the highest examples. Below these, the one who relied on a single sword on horseback hated hearing the teachings of Confucian books; the one at Jinyang who incurred the disgrace of submitting as a subject to foreign captors [?] thereby forfeited the righteousness of his army; and at Chenqiao, the troops turned their weapons against their ruler, sweeping the cardinal bonds of order into the dust. Yet all were able to possess all under Heaven in glory, and their dynastic fortunes endured for several hundred years. Must they necessarily all have attained this by possessing the Way? The one who came in from Linzi and quelled disorder within the palace could not himself escape extravagance and self-indulgence; the one who rose amid the pacification of calamity [?] and continued the succession of the fire-associated Song dynasty likewise failed to escape the habits of commonplace Confucians. Yet both brought order out of chaos and personally achieved a dynastic restoration. Why was this so?
As for attaining sagehood or worthiness through learning, the figures in the transmission of the Way [□] stand as the highest examples. Below these, the one who studied Heaven and humanity perhaps [□] amid the mysteries of yin and yang; the one who wrote Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao) perhaps neglected the work of investigating things and extending knowledge; and entering official service under the non-Han Yuan entailed compromising oneself. These were all celebrated Confucians of their times who revered the learning of the sages. Could there have been something about the Way that they had not heard? The one who, following the proscription of ‘spurious learning,’ wished to be a loyal servant of Master Zhu still did not clearly understand the distinction between preserving the mind and extending knowledge. The one who, during the Jingkang era, alone obtained the authentic transmission of Master Cheng likewise failed to discern the critical moment for taking office or retiring, withdrawing or accepting service. Yet all rendered meritorious service through teaching and study, and the Way depended upon them to keep it from falling into oblivion. Why was this so? Or did they possess other qualities deserving recognition? Now, when the dynastic succession is rightly established above, and the transmission of the Way is made clear among…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
下二者世所須也然不知得國者如何
而可以祈天永命傳道者如何而可以
超凡入聖與古之賢君醇儒之有得於
此者不知何者可爲法與試一言之
問
國家經費仰給東南而戍兵盛於西北迺自
古記之矣今東南連歲災傷民力罄竭
非昔之東南矣承平日久有兵之名而
反受兵之害此二策者不可不熟計之
===
且夫漢漕之初歲數十餘萬而足至武
帝益而爲六百萬乃昭帝之初一年而
盡減之今天下晏然無事而公私之用
常患其不足況可得而盡減者邪唐宋
之季兵數患多而疲耗驕惰爲害於民
今計之
國初則一衛僅及其半或什二三
朝廷非不屢遣使清勾而法司往往謫有罪
以戍守而兵數猶不能復其舊□諸辟
punctuated:
下，二者世所須也。然不知得國者如何而可以祈天永命，傳道者如何而可以超凡入聖與？古之賢君醇儒之有得於此者，不知何者可爲法與？試一言之。

問：國家經費仰給東南，而戍兵盛於西北，迺自古記之矣。今東南連歲災傷，民力罄竭，非昔之東南矣。承平日久，有兵之名，而反受兵之害，此二策者不可不熟計之。且夫漢漕之初，歲數十餘萬而足；至武帝，益而爲六百萬；乃昭帝之初，一年而盡減之。今天下晏然無事，而公私之用常患其不足，況可得而盡減者邪？唐宋之季，兵數患多，而疲耗驕惰，爲害於民。今計之國初，則一衛僅及其半，或什二三。朝廷非不屢遣使清勾，而法司往往謫有罪以戍守，而兵數猶不能復其舊，□諸辟
translation_en:
…below: both are necessary to the world. Yet how can those who obtain rulership pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate, and how can those who transmit the Way transcend the ordinary and enter sagehood? Among the worthy rulers and pure Confucian scholars of antiquity who attained something in this regard, which may serve as models? Offer an account of this.

Question: The state depends upon the southeast for its regular expenditures, while its garrison troops are concentrated in the northwest: this has been recorded since antiquity. Now the southeast has suffered disasters year after year, and the people's resources are utterly exhausted; it is no longer the southeast of former times. After a long period of peace, we have troops in name, yet instead suffer the harm they cause. These two matters of policy demand careful consideration.

When grain transport began under the Han, an annual quantity of several hundred thousand sufficed. Under Emperor Wu it increased to six million; yet at the beginning of Emperor Zhao's reign, the entire increase was eliminated in a single year. Today all under Heaven is peaceful and free of disturbances, yet resources for public and private expenditure are constantly found insufficient. How, then, could such a complete reduction be achieved? In the final years of the Tang and Song, excessive troop numbers were a source of concern, and the troops' exhaustion, wastefulness, arrogance, and indolence harmed the people. Today, compared with the beginning of our dynasty, a guard has barely half its former complement, or perhaps only two or three tenths. It is not that the court has failed repeatedly to send envoys to investigate the rolls and recover missing soldiers; moreover, the judicial authorities frequently sentence offenders to garrison service. Yet troop numbers still cannot be restored to their former level. [The concluding phrase □諸辟 is unclear: ?]…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
宋而其盈虛多寡又君是不同□也或
欲通海運以寬河漕又或欲舉虞集之
說廣置海田以漸減歲運之數而卒病
於難行何也或欲倣傚韓魏公刺義勇
於陜西之法盡籍四輔之民給之田而
以爲兵可得數十萬以爲如此則幾于
唐府兵之遺制矣又或欲舉富鄭公因
饑募兵之法以爲邊以爲釋一兵而可
得十兵夫爲前之說果無害於民否也
===
之策真無補於官邪夫豈□贅蘇軾諸□
其於當時國計皆有所建明今觀其所
患者似又不在於田之不墾歲□之不
加□何也歐陽脩胡寅之在宋論治與
爲獨詳焉誠如其言則今日惟即其見
在之數亦可使將勇兵强而國威以壯
矣乎諸生皆窮居而有范仲淹之志者
是以執事者願一聞焉
punctuated: 宋，而其盈虛多寡又君是不同□也。或欲通海運以寬河漕，又或欲舉虞集之說，廣置海田，以漸減歲運之數，而卒病於難行，何也？或欲倣傚韓魏公刺義勇於陜西之法，盡籍四輔之民，給之田而以爲兵，可得數十萬，以爲如此則幾于唐府兵之遺制矣。又或欲舉富鄭公因饑募兵之法，以爲邊，以爲釋一兵而可得十兵。夫爲前之說，果無害於民否也？之策真無補於官邪？夫豈□贅蘇軾諸□，其於當時國計皆有所建明。今觀其所患者，似又不在於田之不墾、歲□之不加□，何也？歐陽脩、胡寅之在宋，論治與爲獨詳焉。誠如其言，則今日惟即其見在之數，亦可使將勇兵强，而國威以壯矣乎？諸生皆窮居而有范仲淹之志者，是以執事者願一聞焉。
translation_en: …the Song, yet their surpluses and shortfalls, their greater and smaller numbers, differ in this way [?]. Some propose opening sea transport to ease the burden of grain transport by river. Others propose adopting Yu Ji’s proposal to establish extensive coastal farmland, thereby gradually reducing the amount transported annually. Yet these proposals ultimately founder on the difficulty of implementation. Why is this? Some propose imitating the method of Lord Han of Wei, who tattooed recruits for the volunteer militia in Shaanxi: register all the people of the four regions supporting the capital, give them land, and make them soldiers. Several hundred thousand men could thus be obtained. They believe that this would approximate the surviving institutions of the Tang territorial militia system. Others propose adopting Lord Fu of Zheng’s method of recruiting soldiers during famine, to provide for the frontier [?], believing that for every soldier released, ten soldiers could be obtained. Would carrying out the former proposal truly do no harm to the people? Would the [latter?] policy truly bring no benefit to the authorities? The passage mentioning Su Shi and others is unclear [?]; they all offered constructive proposals concerning the state’s finances in their own times. Yet, looking now at what troubled them, it seems that their concern was neither that land remained uncultivated nor that annual [revenues?] failed to increase [?]. Why is this? During the Song, Ouyang Xiu and Hu Yin discussed governance and its implementation in particular detail [?]. If their statements are indeed sound, could we today, simply using the numbers currently available, likewise make our commanders brave and our troops strong, and thereby enhance the might of the state? You candidates all live in modest circumstances yet possess the aspirations of Fan Zhongyan. For this reason, those administering this examination wish to hear your views.

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
克己復禮爲仁一日克己復禮天下歸仁
焉爲仁由己而由人乎哉
何維□
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔禮欠缺處爲己私占去分數故已克禮便復意思甚明塲中類不能知此〕
作獨能道到□□一日克己復禮天下歸仁處
得夫子言意於章句之表殆神解者乎非邪歟
===
考試官教諭童　批〔說理文字似此渾成者絕少必素養有待之士也〕
輸手與
考試官教授趙　批〔孔顏傳授之學□形容特盡宜錄出爲學者式〕
聖人示大賢以仁道之全而尤賛以必爲之勇
焉夫克己復禮則於仁道全矣剋效有必至機
且無難爲之能無勇哉昔吾夫子語顏淵以此
若曰人知仁之當爲而不果於爲者皂以懼其
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「克己復禮爲仁。一日克己復禮，天下歸仁焉。爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？」
何維□
同考試官教諭蕭批〔禮欠缺處，爲己私占去分數，故已克，禮便復，意思甚明。塲中類不能知此〕作獨能道到□□，一日克己復禮、天下歸仁處，得夫子言意於章句之表，殆神解者乎？非邪歟？
考試官教諭童批〔說理文字似此渾成者絕少，必素養有待之士也〕輸手與。
考試官教授趙批〔孔顏傳授之學，□形容特盡，宜錄出爲學者式〕
聖人示大賢以仁道之全，而尤賛以必爲之勇焉。夫克己復禮，則於仁道全矣。剋效有必至，機且無難，爲之能無勇哉？昔吾夫子語顏淵以此，若曰：人知仁之當爲，而不果於爲者，皂以懼其
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“To overcome the self and return to ritual propriety is benevolence. If for one day you overcome the self and return to ritual propriety, all under Heaven will acknowledge your benevolence. Practicing benevolence depends on oneself; could it depend on others?”
He Wei□
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, an Instructor: 〔Where ritual propriety is deficient, selfish desires have occupied its share; thus, once the self is overcome, ritual propriety is restored. The meaning is very clear. Candidates in the examination generally fail to understand this.〕 This composition alone succeeds in expressing it □□. In treating the passage about overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety for one day, and all under Heaven acknowledging one's benevolence, it grasps the Master's meaning beyond the textual commentary. Surely this is an inspired understanding—is it not?
Comment by Examiner Tong, an Instructor: 〔Expositions of principle as seamlessly integrated as this are exceedingly rare. The writer must be a man who has long cultivated himself in readiness for his opportunity.〕 I yield the palm to him [?].
Comment by Examiner Zhao, a Professor: 〔The learning transmitted from Confucius to Yan Hui is □ described with exceptional completeness. This should be recorded as a model for students.〕
The sage showed the great worthy the entirety of the way of benevolence, and especially encouraged in him the courage to put it resolutely into practice. For overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety completes the way of benevolence. The effects of overcoming the self are certain to follow, and the means involve no difficulty [?]; how could one lack the courage to practice it? When our Master spoke of this to Yan Yuan, it was as though he said: People know that benevolence ought to be practiced, yet fail to act decisively, simply because [?] they fear that it …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
罔效而又甚難焉耳予欲知所以爲仁者彼禮
者理之節文而仁之形體也已則吾身私欲與
禮適相反焉必也克去己私以復於禮明健兩
進之餘務屛使邪妄爲之退聽物感不擾之際
自將見眞純於焉復初不失乎天之所以生物
之心且盡乎人之所以爲人之理其斯以爲仁
矣乎然誠能用其力於仁眞積力久以至一日
之間己克而禮以復將見流其仁之聲于體信達
順雖以天下之大遠近不厭矣是何也蓋
===
秉彝好德人心所同天下之廣一日之仁容有
遠焉而未及知可必其矣焉而無不與者矣效
之速而大也何如矧夫仁者身之所由以立其
爲用之急旣非夫人之所可同爲仁者吾之所
當自力其幾微之間亦非夫人之所得與矣是
何也蓋己克以心也禮復以心也事本於心人
不及見可以己得之仁而使之歸與不可以莫
見之事而使之同力矣機之在我而無難也又
何如夫以效可致之於人機實決之于己仁道
punctuated: 罔效而又甚難焉耳。予欲知所以爲仁者，彼禮者，理之節文而仁之形體也。已則吾身私欲，與禮適相反焉。必也克去己私以復於禮，明健兩進之餘，務屛使邪妄爲之退聽；物感不擾之際，自將見眞純於焉復初。不失乎天之所以生物之心，且盡乎人之所以爲人之理，其斯以爲仁矣乎！然誠能用其力於仁，眞積力久，以至一日之間己克而禮以復，將見流其仁之聲于體信達順，雖以天下之大，遠近不厭矣。是何也？蓋秉彝好德，人心所同。天下之廣，一日之仁，容有遠焉而未及知，可必其矣焉而無不與者矣。效之速而大也何如！矧夫仁者，身之所由以立，其爲用之急，旣非夫人之所可同；爲仁者，吾之所當自力，其幾微之間，亦非夫人之所得與矣。是何也？蓋己克以心也，禮復以心也。事本於心，人不及見，可以己得之仁而使之歸與，不可以莫見之事而使之同力矣。機之在我而無難也又何如！夫以效可致之於人，機實決之于己，仁道
translation_en:
…that it will yield no results and will also be exceedingly difficult. I wish to understand how to practice benevolence. Ritual propriety is the articulated pattern of principle and the embodied form of benevolence. The self [?] consists of the private desires within us, which stand directly opposed to ritual propriety. One must overcome selfish desires and return to ritual propriety. As understanding and strength advance together, one must banish deviant and deluded impulses, making them withdraw and submit. When the influence of external things no longer disturbs us, we shall naturally see our true and pure nature restored to its original state. Neither losing Heaven’s life-giving heart nor failing to fulfill the principle by which human beings are human: would this not constitute benevolence?

If one can truly devote one’s strength to benevolence, accumulating genuine effort over a long period, until the day when the self is overcome and ritual propriety restored, one will see one’s reputation for benevolence spread through embodying trustworthiness and extending harmony. Vast though the world is, people near and far will never tire of it. Why is this? Because holding fast to enduring moral norms and loving virtue are common to all human hearts. Across the breadth of the world, there may be distant people who have not yet learned of this single day’s achievement of benevolence; yet one can be certain that none will withhold their approval [?]. How swift and far-reaching its effects!

Moreover, benevolence is that by which one establishes oneself. The urgency of putting it into practice is something others cannot share on one’s behalf. Practicing benevolence requires one’s own exertion; in its subtlest workings, others likewise cannot take part. Why is this? Because overcoming the self is accomplished through the heart, and restoring ritual propriety is accomplished through the heart. The undertaking originates in the heart, where others cannot see it. Through the benevolence one has attained oneself, one can bring others to acknowledge and approve it; but one cannot make them share the effort in an undertaking invisible to them. How entirely its decisive impulse lies within oneself, and how free it is of difficulty! Since its effects can reach others, while its decisive impulse is determined by oneself, the Way of benevolence…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
雖大爲之要亦無甚難也子亦何憚而不勇爲
之哉雖然亦在人也聖門諸賢問仁者多矣雖
隨其資性各有所得然未有若語顏子者端的
而又明備焉豈非以其學焉已近可以語之以
上而望其必成者乎若顏曰無難則曰必效而
可勇以爲之則子貢樊遲之徒皆得以與於此
矣而何爲未達一間獨一回也哉故曰亦在人
也
脩身以道脩道以仁
同考試官教諭孫　批意到詞精乃理學之
深者佳士佳士
同考試官教諭鄭　批此篇乃孔門明德新民
之學此二句又一篇體要義理至大而極精
非平日真有得者不能作此作發揮真切句從
心出是能用力於其仁者錄之不徒以文
考試官教諭童　批理明氣昌發揮近仁
處無遺誠擅場之作
劉第
punctuated:
雖大，爲之要亦無甚難也。子亦何憚而不勇爲之哉？雖然，亦在人也。聖門諸賢問仁者多矣，雖隨其資性各有所得，然未有若語顏子者端的而又明備焉。豈非以其學焉已近，可以語之以上而望其必成者乎？若顏曰無難，則曰必效而可勇以爲之，則子貢、樊遲之徒皆得以與於此矣，而何爲未達一間，獨一回也哉？故曰亦在人也。

脩身以道，脩道以仁。

同考試官教諭孫批：意到詞精，乃理學之深者。佳士！佳士！

同考試官教諭鄭批：此篇乃孔門明德新民之學，此二句又一篇體要，義理至大而極精，非平日真有得者不能作。此作發揮真切，句從心出，是能用力於其仁者。錄之不徒以文。

考試官教諭童批：理明氣昌，發揮近仁處無遺，誠擅場之作。

劉第
translation_en:
…Although benevolence is vast, the essentials of practicing it present no great difficulty. What, then, do you fear, that you do not boldly put it into practice? Even so, it also depends on the person. Many worthy disciples in the Sage’s school asked about benevolence. Although each gained something suited to his disposition and capacities, none received instruction as pointed, clear, and comprehensive as that given to Master Yan. Was this not because his learning had already brought him close, so that he could be instructed in higher matters and expected surely to succeed? If, as with Yan, one says there is no difficulty, and then says that results are assured and one can boldly undertake it [?], then disciples such as Zigong and Fan Chi could all participate in this. Why, then, was Hui alone but a single step short of attainment? Thus I say: it also depends on the person.

“Cultivate oneself through the Way; cultivate the Way through benevolence.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: The ideas are fully realized and the language refined. Here is someone deeply versed in the learning of principle. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: This chapter concerns the learning of manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people in the school of Confucius. These two sentences, moreover, embody the essentials of the entire chapter. Their principles are supremely vast and exceedingly subtle; only someone who has truly grasped them through sustained study could compose such an essay. Its exposition is genuine and precise, and every sentence comes from the heart. This is someone capable of applying himself to benevolence. I select him for more than literary merit alone.

Comment by Examiner Tong, Instructor: The principles are clear and the vital force abundant. The exposition leaves nothing unexplained concerning the approach to benevolence. Truly a work that surpasses the field.

Liu Di.

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授趙　批〔謂以道以仁處許明 真切見能修身修道者宜錄〕
中庸推極夫身之所以脩所以端人君出治之
本也蓋仁以貫道脩身之要具是矣出治者可
不先於是以立其本哉此夫子致望魯哀公中
庸引之以明費隱者也其意若曰古之明王之
所以致盛治於天下也無他道焉本之身以制
政焉爾矣是故以人立政而身焉爲之則慾欲
脩之使其中正明粹而足以爲鑑別之地其必
以道乎蓋道者天下所共由而身之所由以管
攝者也必也表彝常以爲度而凡居身臨物盡
之而弗虧本倫理以求端而凡制行飭躬遵之
而罔越以至一言一動之微莫不各循當然之
則將見雖然內出者閑而之正也有其準紛然
外至者約而之中也得其機身其可得而脩矣
夫以身取人而道焉爲之的茲欲脩之使其真
純完美而足以豫脩省之基又必以仁乎蓋仁
者人心之生理而道之切近精實處也必也洽
punctuated:
考試官教授趙，批〔謂以道以仁處許明，真切，見能修身修道者，宜錄。〕

中庸推極夫身之所以脩、所以端，人君出治之本也。蓋仁以貫道，脩身之要具是矣。出治者可不先於是以立其本哉？此夫子致望魯哀公，中庸引之以明費隱者也。其意若曰：古之明王之所以致盛治於天下也，無他道焉，本之身以制政焉爾矣。是故以人立政，而身焉爲之則，慾欲脩之，使其中正明粹而足以爲鑑別之地，其必以道乎？蓋道者，天下所共由，而身之所由以管攝者也。必也表彝常以爲度，而凡居身臨物盡之而弗虧；本倫理以求端，而凡制行飭躬遵之而罔越。以至一言一動之微，莫不各循當然之則。將見雖然內出者，閑而之正也有其準；紛然外至者，約而之中也得其機。身其可得而脩矣。夫以身取人，而道焉爲之的，茲欲脩之，使其真純完美而足以豫脩省之基，又必以仁乎？蓋仁者，人心之生理，而道之切近精實處也。必也洽
translation_en:
Examiner Zhao, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔The passages discussing “through the Way” and “through benevolence” are clear [?] and incisive. They reveal someone capable of cultivating himself and cultivating the Way; this answer merits inclusion.〕

The Doctrine of the Mean explores to the utmost the means by which the person is cultivated and set upright: this is the foundation from which a ruler brings forth good government. Benevolence runs through the Way, and herein lie all the essentials of self-cultivation. Can one who brings forth good government fail first to establish his foundation here? This is what the Master hoped for from Duke Ai of Lu, and what the Doctrine of the Mean cites to illuminate the Way’s pervasive workings and hidden subtlety. Its meaning is as follows: the enlightened kings of antiquity had no other way of bringing flourishing government to all under Heaven. They simply took their own persons as the foundation for governing.

Thus, government is established through men, and one’s own person supplies the standard. If one wishes [?] to cultivate it, making it balanced, upright, luminous, and pure, and sufficient to serve as the basis for discerning men’s qualities, must this not be done through the Way? The Way is what all under Heaven follow, and that by which one’s person is governed and held in order. One must uphold the constant norms as one’s measure, fulfilling them without deficiency in all one’s personal conduct and dealings with things; one must seek the starting point in the principles of human relationships, following them without transgression in regulating one’s conduct and disciplining oneself. Even the smallest word or movement must follow its proper rule. Then one will see that whatever issues from within [?] has a standard by which it is restrained and directed toward correctness; whatever arrives from without in profusion can be brought into order and directed toward due balance through a grasp of the crucial point. Thus can one’s person be cultivated.

Now, in selecting men by reference to one’s own person, the Way serves as the criterion. If one wishes to cultivate it, making it genuine, pure, complete, and perfect, and sufficient to prepare the foundation for cultivation and self-examination, must this not also be done through benevolence? Benevolence is the life-giving principle of the human heart and the most immediate, essential, and substantial aspect of the Way. One must therefore suffuse …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
恩意於五常之中於以懋一德而盡吾性敦至
理於庸行之際於以管大道以歸一誠凡其纖
悉者之數施皆此謫然者之發越將見親疎同
愛既不使之散漫不倫蹈迪有歸亦不至於虛
虛無物道其可得而脩矣是則以仁則道立矣
以道則身脩矣以是身而取人而行政又何難
於致治哉雖然此非哀公之事也哀公制於二
桓政柄且不在已雖欲脩之爲之亦將何以藉
手邪况乎忘父母之大感而僭行郊祀與周室
===
之淩夷而不脩覲禮於父子君臣之倫一不能盡
道之大綱廢矣何有於仁又何能於政邪夫子
此言固以俟之後聖焉已矣
見其禮而知其政聞其樂而知其德由百
世之後等百世之王莫之能違也自生民
以來未有夫子也
尚維持
考試官教諭董 批〔子貢善觀聖人典所以〕
推尊之意此卷獨說得明白劃切准式
punctuated:
恩意於五常之中，於以懋一德而盡吾性；敦至理於庸行之際，於以管大道以歸一誠。凡其纖悉者之數施，皆此謫然者之發越。將見親疎同愛，既不使之散漫不倫；蹈迪有歸，亦不至於虛虛無物。道其可得而脩矣。是則以仁則道立矣，以道則身脩矣。以是身而取人而行政，又何難於致治哉？雖然，此非哀公之事也。哀公制於二桓，政柄且不在已，雖欲脩之爲之，亦將何以藉手邪？况乎忘父母之大感，而僭行郊祀；與周室之淩夷，而不脩覲禮。於父子君臣之倫，一不能盡，道之大綱廢矣，何有於仁，又何能於政邪？夫子此言，固以俟之後聖焉已矣。
見其禮而知其政，聞其樂而知其德。由百世之後，等百世之王，莫之能違也。自生民以來，未有夫子也。
尚維持
考試官教諭董，批〔子貢善觀聖人典所以〕推尊之意，此卷獨說得明白劃切，准式。
translation_en:
…benevolent feeling within the Five Constant Virtues, thereby cultivating a unified virtue and fully realizing our nature; firmly establishing the highest principles in everyday conduct, thereby encompassing the Great Way and bringing it back to a single sincerity. All its repeated manifestations, down to the smallest detail, issue from this inner quality [?]. We shall then see affection extended alike to those close and distant, without allowing it to become indiscriminate or disregard proper relationships; conduct will have a definite direction, without lapsing into empty nothingness. The Way can thus be cultivated. Through benevolence, the Way is established; through the Way, the person is cultivated. With oneself thus cultivated, what difficulty could there be in selecting worthy people, conducting government, and attaining good order?
Yet this was not something Duke Ai could accomplish. Duke Ai was controlled by the two Huan houses [?], and the reins of government were not even in his own hands. Even if he wished to cultivate himself and put this into practice, what means would he have at his disposal? Moreover, he forgot the profound feeling owed to his parents and presumptuously performed the suburban sacrifice; amid the decline of the Zhou royal house, he failed to observe the rites of court audience. He could not fully discharge even one of the relationships between father and son or ruler and minister. With the great framework of the Way abandoned, what benevolence could he possess, and what could he accomplish in government? These words of the Master were surely intended simply to await a sage of a later age.
“By observing their rites, one knows their government; by hearing their music, one knows their virtue. From a hundred generations later, one can appraise the kings of a hundred generations, and none can escape this judgment. Since humankind first came into being, there has never been anyone like the Master.”
Shang Weichi.
Comment by Examiner Dong, Instructor: “Zigong was skilled at discerning the sage [the wording here is doubtful] and the intention behind his exaltation of him. This essay alone explains this clearly and precisely. Accepted as a model.”

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授趙　批此題子貢語意全重
在德政所以必言禮樂者只爲德政與百王
俱往無從得知借其所遺禮樂以考定之耳
若吾夫子則子貢所親炙德政種種在目何
須禮樂人所云不違是百王後劣不能違我
則上等字方有着落場中作者概認不□講
不違類漫述知政知德講夫子孛孛扯見證
聞樂殊失題旨此作獨能超悟且言政以及
其斟酌四代言德必及其宗主萬世而歸
之聖人所遇之時方結得吾夫子兩盛□策
噫子殆智足以知聖人者
===
賢者言古人之情見于制而因以稽聖人之德
盛焉夫禮樂所以志德政者也稽之則其情見
矣然獨盛者又孰有過於孔子哉昔子思子孫
丑之意蓋謂論人固難而論聖人尤難我之謂
夫子非夷尹所能班者豈獨宰我曾及之哉昔
者子貢亦有言曰禮以飾政者也古之人與其
政往矣似難得其經綸之詳也然治定而制者
punctuated:
考試官教授趙批：此題子貢語意全重在德政，所以必言禮樂者，只爲德政與百王俱往，無從得知，借其所遺禮樂以考定之耳。若吾夫子，則子貢所親炙，德政種種在目，何須禮樂？人所云不違，是百王後劣不能違我，則上等字方有着落。場中作者概認不□講不違，類漫述知政知德；講夫子，孛孛扯見證聞樂，殊失題旨。此作獨能超悟，且言政以及其斟酌四代，言德必及其宗主萬世，而歸之聖人所遇之時，方結得吾夫子兩盛□策。噫！子殆智足以知聖人者。

賢者言古人之情見于制，而因以稽聖人之德盛焉。夫禮樂所以志德政者也，稽之則其情見矣。然獨盛者，又孰有過於孔子哉？昔子思子孫丑之意，蓋謂論人固難，而論聖人尤難。我之謂夫子非夷尹所能班者，豈獨宰我曾及之哉？昔者子貢亦有言曰：「禮以飾政者也。古之人與其政往矣，似難得其經綸之詳也。然治定而制者
translation_en:
Examiner Zhao, an Instructor, comments: In this topic, the entire emphasis of Zigong’s words lies in virtue and government. The reason he must speak of rites and music is simply that the virtue and government of the kings of a hundred generations have passed away with them and cannot be known directly; one must examine and assess them through the rites and music they left behind. Our Master, however, was someone from whom Zigong received instruction personally: every aspect of his virtue and government was before Zigong’s eyes. What need was there for rites and music? What is called “not departing from” means that the kings of a hundred generations, being inferior, could not surpass me [?]; only then does the preceding word “rank” have a definite application. The candidates in the examination hall generally misconstrue this [illegible passage] in explaining “not departing from” [?], mostly discoursing vaguely on knowing government and knowing virtue. When discussing the Master, they confusedly drag in “seeing,” “testimony,” and “hearing music” [?], quite missing the topic’s purport. This composition alone shows exceptional understanding. Moreover, in speaking of government, it reaches his considered selection from the four dynasties; in speaking of virtue, it necessarily addresses his being the guiding authority for ten thousand generations. It then relates these to the age in which the sage lived. Only thus does it bring the two excellences of our Master to a conclusion [text doubtful and partly illegible]. Ah! You are surely one whose wisdom suffices to know the sage.

The worthy speaks of how the true character of the ancients appears in their institutions, and uses these to examine the fullness of the sage’s virtue. Rites and music are what record virtue and government; by examining them, one can perceive their true character. Yet who could surpass Confucius in singular excellence? Formerly, the intention of “Zisi, Zi, Sunchou” [?] was presumably to say that assessing people is certainly difficult, but assessing a sage is harder still. When I say that our Master could not be ranked alongside Yi and Yin, was Zai Wo alone in having expressed this? Zigong too once said: “Rites give ordered expression to government. The men of antiquity have passed away together with their government, and it seems difficult to recover the details of their ordering of affairs. Yet what was instituted once good order had been established…”

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
有禮在焉見其禮不可以知其政乎樂以彰德
者也古之人與其德亡矣似難悉其心術之微
也然功成而作者有樂在焉聞其樂不可以知
其德乎蓋德政雖寓于制作之中而禮樂實發
其精微之蘊矣是以我也由百世之後執此仰
稽於隆古之前但見盡百世之王優劣莫逭於
品量之下而因見夫子之不可及焉是何也蓋
以百王而較百王則百王自有其等以百王
較吾夫子則夫子獨出其類自有生民以來
===
閒盡制而王盡道而聖者雖不乏人〔至如夫〕
之聖則又達乎天地冠乎古今也而莫與〔與並〕
來動和之化捷應於得邦家之時禮酌四代
王且在其範圍焉此政之餘蓋莫有遺政者矣
吾道一貫之神不涉乎思勉之迹爰垂萬世斯
文實賴以宗主焉此德之外蓋莫有遺德者矣
謂爲獨盛豈不信與夫即子貢此言觀之則晏
尹何人也顧可以班於孔子哉我之所以願學
厥有由矣抑考聖人無不同之心則無不同之
punctuated:
有禮在焉，見其禮，不可以知其政乎？樂以彰德者也。古之人與其德亡矣，似難悉其心術之微也。然功成而作者，有樂在焉，聞其樂，不可以知其德乎？蓋德政雖寓于制作之中，而禮樂實發其精微之蘊矣。是以我也，由百世之後，執此仰稽於隆古之前，但見盡百世之王，優劣莫逭於品量之下，而因見夫子之不可及焉。是何也？蓋以百王而較百王，則百王自有其等；以百王較吾夫子，則夫子獨出其類。自有生民以來，閒盡制而王、盡道而聖者，雖不乏人，〔至如夫〕之聖，則又達乎天地，冠乎古今也，而莫與〔與並〕。來動和之化，捷應於得邦家之時，禮酌四代，王且在其範圍焉。此政之餘，蓋莫有遺政者矣。吾道一貫之神，不涉乎思勉之迹，爰垂萬世，斯文實賴以宗主焉。此德之外，蓋莫有遺德者矣。謂爲獨盛，豈不信與？」
夫即子貢此言觀之，則晏尹何人也，顧可以班於孔子哉？我之所以願學，厥有由矣。抑考聖人無不同之心，則無不同之
translation_en:
…rites remain. By observing their rites, can one not know their government? Music serves to manifest virtue. The men of antiquity and their virtue have passed away, and it seems difficult to comprehend fully the subtleties of their minds. Yet the music they composed when their achievements were complete remains. By hearing their music, can one not know their virtue? For although virtue and government are embodied in institutions, rites and music reveal their most subtle depths. Thus, living a hundred generations later, I take these as evidence and look back to examine remote antiquity. I find that none of the kings of those hundred generations, whether superior or inferior, escapes assessment; and through this I perceive that the Master cannot be equaled. Why is this? When the kings are compared with one another, they naturally fall into ranks; but when they are compared with our Master, he alone surpasses his kind. Since humankind first came into being, there have been no few who became kings by fully establishing institutions, or sages by fully realizing the Way [?]. 〔As for the Master’s [?]〕 sageliness, it reaches throughout Heaven and Earth and stands foremost in antiquity and the present, with none 〔to equal him [?]〕. His transforming influence, drawing people to him and moving them to harmony [?], would take effect immediately upon his obtaining a state or ruling house. His rites draw judiciously upon the four dynasties, and even their kings fall within his compass. Beyond this government, no aspect of government remains unaccounted for. The wondrous efficacy of ‘my Way, threaded through by a single principle’ bears no trace of deliberation or effort. Handed down through ten thousand generations, it is what this cultural tradition truly relies upon as its guiding authority. Beyond this virtue, no aspect of virtue remains unaccounted for. Is it not indeed true to call him uniquely preeminent?”
Now, considered in light of these words of Zigong, who are Yan and Yin [?], that they could be ranked alongside Kongzi? My wish to learn from him certainly has its grounds. Yet, if we examine how the sages’ minds are invariably alike, then there can be no difference in their…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
德德而不同不足以爲聖人矣是故伏羲神農
黃帝堯舜禹湯文武周公以及孔子一也其爲
德同其所以爲政則因時創制結繩而書
契非備也禪繼非順而征誅非僭也制作非近
而論述非遠也亦爲其所得爲而已矣使堯舜
數聖人而當孔子之時則亦能爲孔子之事此
無他道在故也故曰聖人無優劣
易
九五丼節吉往有尚
===
許廷用
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔節道之士制數而德行二者所以品節人之性情使合於中大〕
抵人情便肆惡檢便肆情之過惡含於性矣之不
及聖人乃爲之節制使合於中其先便與惡
生於過與不及今既得中本原復而眞好出
矣故丼節丼字不獨在上所行直欲驗之人
心之說服如五味和而人丼美之然也此作
能道盡始有得於中正之通與
punctuated:
德。德而不同，不足以爲聖人矣。是故伏羲、神農、黃帝、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周公以及孔子，一也。其爲德同，其所以爲政，則因時創制。結繩而書契，非備也；禪繼非順，而征誅非僭也；制作非近，而論述非遠也。亦爲其所得爲而已矣。使堯舜數聖人而當孔子之時，則亦能爲孔子之事。此無他，道在故也。故曰：「聖人無優劣。」
《易》
九五，丼節，吉，往有尚。
許廷用
同考試官教諭蕭，批〔節道之士，制數而德行，二者所以品節人之性情，使合於中。大〕抵人情便肆惡檢，便肆，情之過；惡含於性矣之不及。聖人乃爲之節制，使合於中。其先便與惡，生於過與不及；今既得中，本原復而眞好出矣。故丼節，丼字不獨在上所行，直欲驗之人心之說服，如五味和而人丼美之然也。此作能道盡，始有得於中正之通與？
translation_en:
…virtue. If their virtue differed, they would not qualify as sages. Thus Fuxi, Shennong, Huangdi, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius are one. Their virtue was the same; in governing, however, they established institutions according to their times. The transition from knotted cords to written contracts was not a matter of greater completeness. Succession by abdication was not inherently compliant with the proper order, nor were punitive campaigns and executions usurpation. Creating institutions was not shortsighted, nor was expounding inherited teachings remote from practical affairs. They merely did what their circumstances allowed them to do. Had Yao, Shun, and the other sages lived in Confucius’s time, they too could have done what Confucius did. There is no other reason for this: the Way was present in them. Thus it is said: “Among sages there is no superiority or inferiority.”
Book of Changes
Nine in the fifth place: Sweet restraint brings good fortune. Going forward brings esteem.
Xu Tingyong
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔In the way of restraint, “the scholar” [?], numerical regulations, and virtuous conduct—these two serve to regulate people’s natural dispositions and feelings, bringing them into accord with the mean.〕 Generally, human feelings favor license and dislike restraint. Favoring license is an excess of feeling; the passage concerning dislike and deficiency in one’s nature is garbled [?]. The sage therefore imposes restraint to bring them into accord with the mean. Their earlier preferences and aversions arose from excess and deficiency. Now that the mean has been attained, the original foundation is restored and true preferences emerge. Thus, in “sweet restraint,” the word “sweet” does not refer solely to what those above practice: it must be verified in people’s heartfelt acceptance, just as people find a harmonious blend of the five flavors sweet and pleasing. This composition fully expresses this meaning. Has it thereby attained an understanding of how centrality and correctness bring things into accord?

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭童　批〔說出節道之宜民而能致治意趣宛然且詞健格高非苟作者〕
〔可錄〕
考試官教授趙　批〔潔淨精粹易義必如此乃佳〕
爻以陽居尊聖人著其節道之善而示以治道
之成焉夫節而能甘可謂善矣則夫吉而有尚
寧非治道之成哉周公繫其辭如此且節
五居卦之尊為節之主是當位而中正者也
===
當位則大觀在上而率世罔敢或撓中正則
德藴中而範物為之有本是以其節天下也
革惟順事以平施齊其政不異其俗損益一從
時以達變脩其教靡拂于經自一身以及兆民
制度章程軌迹夷易不外乎會通典禮之常由
朝廷以達邦國體統等威成法昭明惟合乎大
中至正之矩夫節之甘也如此而其占曰吉曰
往有尚焉蓋任知經始皆圖贊襄之累通變宜
民者茂圖大之功將見教立表端絕無微不
punctuated:
考試官教諭童，批〔說出節道之宜民而能致治，意趣宛然，且詞健格高，非苟作者〕〔可錄〕。
考試官教授趙，批〔潔淨精粹，易義必如此乃佳〕。
爻以陽居尊，聖人著其節道之善，而示以治道之成焉。夫節而能甘，可謂善矣，則夫吉而有尚，寧非治道之成哉？周公繫其辭如此。且節五居卦之尊，為節之主，是當位而中正者也。當位則大觀在上，而率世罔敢或撓；中正則德藴中，而範物為之有本。是以其節天下也，革惟順事以平施，齊其政，不異其俗；損益一從時以達變，脩其教，靡拂于經。自一身以及兆民，制度章程，軌迹夷易，不外乎會通典禮之常；由朝廷以達邦國，體統等威，成法昭明，惟合乎大中至正之矩。夫節之甘也如此，而其占曰吉，曰往有尚焉。蓋任知經始，皆圖贊襄之累，通變宜民者，茂圖大之功。將見教立表端，絕無微不
translation_en:
Examiner Tong, Instructor, comments: 〔The answer brings out how the way of regulation benefits the people and achieves good government. Its meaning and tenor emerge distinctly; moreover, its language is vigorous and its style elevated. This is no careless composition.〕〔Worthy of inclusion.〕
Examiner Zhao, Professor, comments: 〔Clean, pure, refined, and substantial: an exposition of the Book of Changes must be like this to be excellent.〕
The line, being yang and occupying the honored position, allows the sage to reveal the excellence of its way of regulation and to show the consummation of good government. Regulation that can be sweet may indeed be called excellent. Thus, when it brings good fortune and esteem for going forward, is this not the consummation of good government? Such were the words the Duke of Zhou appended to the line. Moreover, the fifth line of Regulation occupies the honored position in the hexagram and presides over regulation: it occupies its proper place and is central and correct. Occupying its proper place, it stands above as a grand example and leads the world, with none daring to obstruct it. Being central and correct, it holds virtue within, providing a foundation for setting standards for all things.
Thus, in regulating all under Heaven, it makes changes only in accordance with circumstances, applying them equitably; it brings government into order without altering local customs. Its reductions and additions accord entirely with the times, accommodating change; it cultivates instruction without contravening enduring principles. From the ruler’s own person to the myriad people, institutions, regulations, and established practices are straightforward and accessible, remaining within the constant norms of statutes and rites comprehensively understood. From the court to the various states, the governing order, distinctions of rank and dignity, and established laws are clear and manifest, conforming solely to the standards of supreme balance and utmost correctness.
Such is the sweetness of regulation, and its prognostication accordingly says “good fortune” and “going forward brings esteem.” For employing wisdom in laying foundations always seeks the accumulated assistance of others [?]; those who accommodate change and benefit the people bring to fullness the achievement of great designs [?]. We shall see instruction established and the example set aright, with absolutely nothing, however minute, failing to …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
之嬀充然王制之盡善禮達分定無作好作惡
之議允矣民過之可寡制度章程推無不準一
人達之天下遵其路也體統等威動無不化大
道之公萬方爲之程也言而有尚又如此是則
非節之難也非節之爲難非節之難也德位
兼備之爲難夫君治道之成有自然哉抑人有
言非常之原黎民懼焉故協民之衷乃所以裔
治若上非天時下非地利中非民則方非時
而以言治者誣也是故備物制用立成器以
===
天下利聖人馭治之道大矣末世之務動下
民封禪興而海内耗新法作而天下擾始不
易哉
夫易何爲者也夫易開物成務冒天下之
道如斯而已者也是故聖人以通天下之
志以定天下之業以斷天下之疑
何維
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔聖人作易以前民用〕
〔厥功大矣此作敷敍既明而理致尤渾融誠〕
punctuated:
之嬀，充然王制之盡善；禮達分定，無作好作惡之議，允矣民過之可寡。制度章程，推無不準，一人達之天下，遵其路也；體統等威，動無不化，大道之公，萬方爲之程也。言而有尚，又如此。是則非節之難也，非節之爲難，非節之難也，德位兼備之爲難。夫君治道之成，有自然哉？抑人有言：「非常之原，黎民懼焉。」故協民之衷，乃所以裔治。若上非天時，下非地利，中非民則，方非時，而以言治者，誣也。是故備物制用，立成器以天下利，聖人馭治之道大矣！末世之務，動下民，封禪興而海内耗，新法作而天下擾，始不易哉！
夫易何爲者也？夫易開物成務，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。是故聖人以通天下之志，以定天下之業，以斷天下之疑。
何維
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔聖人作易以前民用〕〔厥功大矣。此作敷敍既明，而理致尤渾融，誠〕
translation_en:
…[opening characters unclear: 之嬀, ?], fully realizing the perfection of royal institutions. Ritual prevails and distinctions are settled; there is no occasion to criticize arbitrary favor or aversion, and the people's transgressions can indeed be few. Institutions and regulations provide a standard wherever they are extended: the one ruler extends them throughout the realm, and all follow their path. The ordering of authority and the gradations of dignity transform all wherever they operate: the impartiality of the Great Way becomes a model for every region. That words should win esteem [?] is likewise illustrated here. Thus, it is not regulation that is difficult; it is not regulation that presents the difficulty; it is not regulation that is difficult. What is difficult is possessing both virtue and position. Can a ruler's achievement of good government come about of itself? Yet someone has said, “At the inception of extraordinary undertakings, the common people are afraid.” Thus, harmonizing with the people's innermost sentiments is the means of extending good government [?]. If above one disregards Heaven's seasons, below one disregards the advantages of the land, and in between one disregards the people's norms, acting at an unsuitable time [?], then to speak of governing thereby is a falsehood. Therefore, by providing things and regulating their use, and establishing finished implements for the benefit of the realm [?], the sages demonstrate the greatness of their way of governing! The undertakings of declining ages unsettle the common people: the institution of the feng and shan sacrifices exhausted the resources of the empire, and the introduction of the New Policies threw the realm into turmoil. Was making a beginning not difficult indeed [?]!
What does the Book of Changes do? The Book of Changes discloses things, brings undertakings to completion, and encompasses the Way of all under Heaven: this is all it does. Thus the sages use it to comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven, to settle the undertakings of all under Heaven, and to resolve the doubts of all under Heaven.
He Wei
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: 〔The sages composed the Book of Changes to guide the people's use of things.〕〔Great indeed was their achievement! This composition is clear in its exposition, and its reasoning is especially well integrated. Truly…〕

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
括必學易而有得者錄之
考試官教諭童　批〔易備羣用之妙作者類能知之但其體紛而不整其意斷而不屬殊無可觀獨此作得其旨歸而且端潔通暢必深於易之士也允宜高薦〕
考試官教授趙　批〔易道之大此作盡之匪是無以崇易教者宜表出以式〕
易以前民用則易固羣用之妙者也是故士
大傳推極易道無非以前民用者也夫聖人
===
發其義也如此其言曰夫自天不愛道而神
生聖人成能而易象作以人知夫易也卦以御
賾爻以觀其動而不知循名以測義原始以要
終夫何為者也蓋事物將至有開必先幾至秘
也而易固開之是晰于未朕察于未形者也天
下之動殊途異致務至紛也而易固成之是利
於攸往妙於致用者也而又函括萬理極其悉
備而不為功綜紀庶倫撰于雜物而不為有易
之為易固如此矣夫唯開物也則昭示詳而將
punctuated:
括，必學易而有得者，錄之。

考試官教諭童，批〔易備羣用之妙，作者類能知之，但其體紛而不整，其意斷而不屬，殊無可觀。獨此作得其旨歸，而且端潔通暢，必深於易之士也，允宜高薦。〕

考試官教授趙，批〔易道之大，此作盡之。匪是，無以崇易教者，宜表出以式。〕

易以前民用，則易固羣用之妙者也。是故士《大傳》推極易道，無非以前民用者也。夫聖人發其義也如此，其言曰：「夫自天不愛道而神生，聖人成能而易象作。」以人知夫易也，卦以御賾，爻以觀其動，而不知循名以測義，原始以要終，夫何為者也？蓋事物將至，有開必先，幾至秘也，而易固開之，是晰于未朕、察于未形者也。天下之動，殊途異致，務至紛也，而易固成之，是利於攸往、妙於致用者也。而又函括萬理，極其悉備而不為功；綜紀庶倫，撰于雜物而不為有。易之為易，固如此矣。夫唯開物也，則昭示詳而將
translation_en:
…comprehensive [?]. This must be someone who has studied the Changes and gained understanding from it. Select this essay.

Examiner Tong, Instructor, comments: 〔The Changes embodies the subtle efficacy of every kind of application. Most writers can recognize this, but their compositions are disordered and ill arranged, their ideas disconnected and incoherent, with scarcely anything worth reading. This essay alone grasps its essential purport and is also disciplined, polished, clear, and fluent. Its author must be a scholar deeply versed in the Changes and certainly deserves a high recommendation.〕

Examiner Zhao, Professor, comments: 〔This essay fully expresses the greatness of the Way of the Changes. Without such writing, there would be no means of exalting its teaching. It should be singled out as a model.〕

The Changes guides the people in their practical undertakings; thus it indeed possesses the subtle efficacy required for every kind of application. Accordingly, the Great Commentary [?], in exploring the Way of the Changes to its utmost, invariably aims to guide the people in their undertakings. Such is the meaning that the sage expounds. Its words say: “Heaven does not withhold the Way, and spiritual powers arise [?]; the sage brings his capacities to fulfillment, and the images of the Changes are produced.” People know [?] that in the Changes the hexagrams govern what is abstruse and the individual lines disclose its movements. Yet if they do not follow the names to fathom their meanings, or trace beginnings to comprehend outcomes, what purpose does this serve?

When events and things are about to arrive, their unfolding necessarily has a precursor. These incipient signs are exceedingly hidden, yet the Changes discloses them: it clarifies what has not yet shown a trace and discerns what has not yet taken form. The movements of all under Heaven take divergent paths toward different ends. Affairs are exceedingly tangled, yet the Changes brings them to completion: it makes whatever course one pursues advantageous and is subtle in its practical efficacy. Moreover, it encompasses the myriad principles, attaining complete comprehensiveness without claiming merit; it orders the many relationships and arranges diverse things without claiming possession. Such indeed is what makes the Changes the Changes. Precisely because it discloses things, its illuminating instruction is detailed and will…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
燦然者矣成務也則舉動一而有亹亹者矣昌
天下之道則稽實待虛於無窮執古御今之不
御者矣是蓋使天下之民外鄙以撤中庸由明
而惠迪從逆之故若或啓之也志有不通乎變
而通之鼓之舞之而盡利盡神之妙若或翼之
也業有不定乎指其所之則向往明而不惑適
其所值則憂患釋而無岐疑有不斷乎是故以
理設而聖人之精以明以人鬼謀而百姓之能
與易斯其至矣抑易本於天毅于地通乎田
===
貢于經緯而以民用卜筮盡之不既小與士
非以彰淺非以晦深故太極者非潛卜筮以
顯也潛非精而顯非迹也楊子雲之玄曰旋其
位而宣其診攘其功而幽其所以然是舍矣功
而愚之民也豈聖人之所爲哉
書
若作酒醴爾惟麴糵若作和羹爾惟鹽梅
劉第
同考試官教諭雍　批〔麴糵作酒醴鹽梅作〕
punctuated:
燦然者矣。成務也，則舉動一而有亹亹者矣。昌天下之道，則稽實待虛於無窮，執古御今之不御者矣。是蓋使天下之民外鄙以撤中庸，由明而惠迪從逆之故，若或啓之也。志有不通乎？變而通之，鼓之舞之，而盡利盡神之妙，若或翼之也。業有不定乎？指其所之，則向往明而不惑；適其所值，則憂患釋而無岐。疑有不斷乎？是故以理設，而聖人之精以明；以人鬼謀，而百姓之能與。易斯其至矣。抑易本於天，毅于地，通乎田，貢于經緯，而以民用卜筮盡之，不既小與？士非以彰淺，非以晦深，故太極者非潛卜筮以顯也，潛非精而顯非迹也。楊子雲之玄曰：「旋其位而宣其診，攘其功而幽其所以然。」是舍矣功而愚之民也，豈聖人之所爲哉？

書
若作酒醴，爾惟麴糵；若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。
劉第
同考試官教諭雍，批〔麴糵作酒醴，鹽梅作〕
translation_en:
…will shine brilliantly. In bringing undertakings to completion, it unifies action and inspires unremitting effort. In making the Way flourish throughout the world, it examines what is actual and awaits what is yet unrealized without limit; it holds to antiquity to govern what in the present remains ungoverned [?]. Thus it enables the people of the world to cast aside what is mean and bring the constant mean into effect [?], proceeding from understanding to follow the right path and comprehend the reasons for compliance and opposition—as though someone were enlightening them. Could their aspirations fail to find expression? Through change it opens a way for them, rousing and inspiring them, fully realizing the marvel of benefit and spiritual efficacy—as though someone were assisting them. Could their undertakings remain unsettled? By indicating where they should go, it makes their direction clear and dispels confusion; by fitting their circumstances, it releases them from anxiety and leaves no divided course. Could their doubts remain unresolved? Thus, through the establishment of principles, the sages’ essential understanding is made clear; through consultation with humans and spirits, the abilities of the common people are brought into play. Here the Changes reaches its utmost perfection.

Yet the Changes is rooted in Heaven, is firm in Earth [?], extends through the fields [?], and contributes to the warp and weft of order [?]. To exhaust its meaning in the people’s use of stalk and turtle-shell divination—is this not to make it altogether too small? The scholar [?] is not shallow through being manifest, nor profound through being obscure. Thus the Great Ultimate is not hidden merely to be revealed through divination [?]; what is hidden is not necessarily the essence, nor what is manifest merely its outward traces. Yang Ziyun’s Supreme Mystery says: “Rotate its positions and make its prognostications known; take its achievements, but conceal the reasons why they are so” [?]. This is to discard its achievements and keep the people ignorant [?]. Could this be what the sages intended?

Documents

“If I were making wine or sweet liquor, you would be the ferment and malt; if I were making a well-seasoned soup, you would be the salt and sour plums.”

Liu Di

Comment by Associate Examiner Yong, Instructor: 〔Ferment and malt make wine and sweet liquor; salt and sour plums make …〕

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
和羨作者類能言之求其能以柔濟剛□□
否意思隱括其間一滚寫出則絕少子□□
之且辭旨簡遠典重疏通知遠而不誣者非
子邪
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔高宗命說訓志本自學之罔顯而來麴蘖鹽梅蓋亦借爲〕
〔父降進學之喻耳作者每每說不到此是篇獨能推〕
明詳盡且辭理該括宜冠多士
考試官教諭童　批〔簡而盡明而順〕
考試官教授趙　批〔高宗命相之意〕
明白簡切宜薦允宜
===
賢之資相臣之訓志兩托物以深致其意焉蓋
君臣之相須以成德猶物理之相資以濟用也
賢王托物以爲喻可謂相信之深者矣昔高宗
之命傅說甚意蓋曰君臣之遂每病於勢分之
隔德業之盛恒資於上下之交爾說之訓于朕
志也抑何所似邪譬之酒醴之作必資乎麴蘖
也爾其爲朕之麴蘖者乎蓋作酒醴者麴多則失
punctuated:
和羨，作者類能言之，求其能以柔濟剛□□否意思隱括其間，一滚寫出，則絕少。子□□之，且辭旨簡遠，典重疏通，知遠而不誣者，非子邪？

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
之苦蘖多則失之甘必甘苦適中而酒斯成也
爾說也啓沃之誠順適於開導之餘勿曰過剛
以逆朕志也誨迪之切謹於朝夕之際無或
過柔以遜朕志也庶乎剛柔相濟猶麴蘖之相
資吾之學可底於顯也不但是也夫和羹之
作必資乎鹽梅也爾其為朕之鹽梅者乎蓋作
羹者鹽過則失之鹹梅過則失之酸必酸鹹適
宜而羹斯和也爾說也知無不言而可焉必
輔之翼之務引君志以道寧也言無不盡而
===
焉必替匡之直之昭乃辟德求無愆也庶乎
否克諧猶鹽梅之相成吾之學不終于廢也
以微物自托於已而以訓志深責於人其言之
懇至如此謂聖人任輔相之道非邪豈于是而
觀高宗之于傳說帝賚于夢形肖于傳巖遇之
奇也與之語爰立作相用之驟也輔德之喻曰
麴蘖鹽梅曰舟楫霖雨不一而足情之孚也遇
之奇則可以驗格天之速用之驟可以觀帝德
之果情之孚則形迹相忘而陋後世矣此其所
punctuated:
之苦，蘖多則失之甘，必甘苦適中而酒斯成也。爾說也，啓沃之誠，順適於開導之餘，勿曰過剛以逆朕志也；誨迪之切，謹於朝夕之際，無或過柔以遜朕志也。庶乎剛柔相濟，猶麴蘖之相資，吾之學可底於顯也。不但是也，夫和羹之作，必資乎鹽梅也。爾其為朕之鹽梅者乎？蓋作羹者，鹽過則失之鹹，梅過則失之酸，必酸鹹適宜而羹斯和也。爾說也，知無不言，而可焉必輔之翼之，務引君志以道寧也；言無不盡，而焉必替，匡之直之，昭乃辟德，求無愆也。庶乎否克諧，猶鹽梅之相成，吾之學不終于廢也。」

translation_en:
…too bitter; too much malt makes it too sweet. Only when sweetness and bitterness are properly balanced does the wine turn out well. You, Yue, must sincerely open and enrich my mind, tempering your guidance with gentleness; do not speak with excessive rigidity and oppose my intentions [?]. Be earnest in instruction and vigilant morning and evening, without becoming excessively yielding and accommodating my intentions. Then firmness and gentleness may complement one another, just as ferment and malt support one another, and my learning may attain clarity. Nor is this all. Preparing a well-balanced soup necessarily requires salt and sour plums. Will you be my salt and sour plums? Too much salt makes soup excessively salty; too many plums make it excessively sour. Only when sourness and saltiness are properly balanced does the soup become harmonious. You, Yue, must speak of everything you know: where something is right, you must support and assist it, striving to guide your ruler’s intentions toward repose in the Way. You must leave nothing unsaid, and where … you must reject it [?], correcting and straightening it, making your sovereign’s virtue manifest and seeking freedom from error. Thus what is wrong may be brought into harmony [?], just as salt and sour plums complete one another, and my learning will not ultimately fall into neglect.”
He entrusted his own case to analogies with humble things, while placing upon another the weighty responsibility of instructing his intentions. His words were earnest and heartfelt to this degree. Could one say that this was not the sage’s way of entrusting responsibility to an assisting minister? Looking here at Gaozong’s dealings with Fu Yue [?]: Heaven bestowed him in a dream, and his likeness was found at Fuyan—extraordinary was their encounter. Gaozong spoke with him and thereupon appointed him chief minister—swift was his employment. As analogies for assistance in cultivating virtue, Gaozong spoke of ferment and malt, salt and sour plums, boats and oars, and timely rain; one example did not suffice—such was the sincerity of their mutual trust. Their extraordinary encounter shows how swiftly he moved Heaven; the speed of the appointment reveals the decisiveness of his imperial virtue. Their sincere mutual trust allowed them to forget distinctions of outward status, putting later ages to shame. This was what enabled them to …

寧曰迪哲然則君道豈易言哉
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日歲月日時
無易百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家用平
