皇太子曰脩己治人之要具載此書帝王之
學貴於知要則是書之旨者也我
成祖之爲聖學心法也則嘗出示翰林學
===
廣矣其言曰帝王之學但得其要筞
行足以爲治此心法之旨者也大一書
謂帝王之要者何也帝王之心是也而
所以操持是心之法綱目具舉要而言之
則敬之一言盡之矣故我
皇上於敬一之箴五箴之註發其蘊焉百餘年
來家齊國治天地位而萬物育斯民優
堯舜之治則亦以我
列聖之於道也得其要而推行之也有其基焉
punctuated: 聖子神孫千萬世道學之淵源者，寔自高皇帝始。執事謂東宮授受尤獨明備者，則列聖繼述之意深矣。是故聖祖之爲昭鑑錄也，則成祖旣廣之而爲文華寶鑑矣。而其授皇太子曰：「脩己治人之要，具載此書。」帝王之學貴於知要，則是書之旨者也。我成祖之爲聖學心法也，則嘗出示翰林學廣矣。其言曰：「帝王之學，但得其要，筞行足以爲治。」此心法之旨者也。大一書謂帝王之要者何也？帝王之心是也。而所以操持是心之法，綱目具舉；要而言之，則敬之一言盡之矣。故我皇上於敬一之箴、五箴之註，發其蘊焉。百餘年來，家齊國治，天地位而萬物育，斯民優堯舜之治，則亦以我列聖之於道也，得其要而推行之也，有其基焉
translation_en: …the wellspring of the Learning of the Way for his sagely sons and divine grandsons through countless generations truly began with Emperor Gao. You, sir, say that its transmission to the heir apparent was especially clear and complete: this shows the profound intention of the successive sage emperors to carry forward their predecessors’ work. Thus, when the sagely founding emperor compiled the Record of the Illustrious Mirror (Zhaojian lu), Chengzu subsequently expanded it into the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian). In presenting it to the imperial heir apparent, he said: “The essentials of cultivating oneself and governing others are fully recorded in this book.” Imperial learning prizes knowing the essentials: that is the purport of this book. When our Chengzu composed the Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), he once brought it out to show the Hanlin scholars [?]. He said: “In imperial learning, one need only grasp its essentials; putting them into practice [?] is sufficient to bring about good government.” This is the purport of the Methods of the Mind. What does the book [?] mean by the essentials of imperial rule? They are the emperor’s mind. As for the methods of maintaining mastery over this mind, both their main principles and their particulars are fully set forth; to state their essence, the single word ‘reverence’ encompasses them all. Thus our reigning emperor brought out their underlying meaning in his Admonition on Unifying through Reverence (Jingyi zhen) and his annotations to the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen). For more than a hundred years, families have been ordered and the state well governed; Heaven and Earth have occupied their proper places, and the myriad things have flourished. These people have enjoyed government surpassing [?] that of Yao and Shun. This too is because our successive sage emperors grasped the essentials of the Way and put them into practice, thereby establishing its foundation…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
爾然則斯道之統在乎上諸臣躬逢其
盛得無有見而知之者乎竊聞之賈誼曰天
下之命繫於太子太子之善莫先於蚤諭
教與選左右也今
宮寮諸臣旣皆出于
聖心之所簡擇而諭教之方宣草茅之所敢與
知然獨無忠愛之心乎蓋嘗伏讀
御製而有以仰窺其萬一矣曰夫敬者存乎
而不忽之謂也一者純乎理而不雜
===
也又曰苟此心忽而不敬則此德豈
而不雜哉故其於箴也求之於
郊求之於
廟求之於
明庭閒居要之亦欲是心之純乎天理而勿貳
勿叁耳其終曰君德旣脩萬邦則正天親
民懷永延厥慶光前垂後綿延蕃盛則我
皇上躬自蹈之德洽神人和于上下有以上慰
祖宗之心而所望於後人以衍無疆之休者亦
punctuated: 爾。然則斯道之統在乎上，諸臣躬逢其盛，得無有見而知之者乎？竊聞之，賈誼曰：「天下之命繫於太子，太子之善莫先於蚤諭教與選左右也。」今宮寮諸臣旣皆出于聖心之所簡擇，而諭教之方，宣草茅之所敢與知，然獨無忠愛之心乎？蓋嘗伏讀御製，而有以仰窺其萬一矣。曰：「夫敬者，存乎而不忽之謂也；一者，純乎理而不雜也。」又曰：「苟此心忽而不敬，則此德豈而不雜哉？」故其於箴也，求之於郊，求之於廟，求之於明庭閒居，要之亦欲是心之純乎天理而勿貳勿叁耳。其終曰：「君德旣脩，萬邦則正；天親民懷，永延厥慶；光前垂後，綿延蕃盛。」則我皇上躬自蹈之，德洽神人，和于上下，有以上慰祖宗之心，而所望於後人以衍無疆之休者亦
translation_en: …and that is all. Thus, if the succession of this Way rests with the sovereign, can there be none among the ministers, personally encountering its flourishing, who see it and thereby understand it? I have humbly heard these words of Jia Yi: “The fate of All-under-Heaven is bound to the heir apparent. In making the heir apparent good, nothing takes precedence over instructing him early and selecting those who attend him.” Now the officials of the heir apparent’s household have all been personally selected by His Majesty. As for the methods of instruction, [the wording concerning whether one outside official service may presume to know of them is doubtful: ?]. Yet could such a person alone lack a heart of loyalty and affection? I have reverently read the imperial writings and thereby gained a glimpse of the smallest part of their meaning. They say: “Reverence means maintaining [attentiveness?] without lapsing into heedlessness; oneness means being pure in principle, without admixture.” They also say: “If this heart becomes heedless and irreverent, how could this virtue … be without admixture [?]?” Thus, in the admonition, this is sought at the suburban sacrifices, in the ancestral temple, in the court, and in private life. In essence, the aim is simply that this heart remain pure in Heaven’s principle, without being divided between two or three objects. Its conclusion reads: “When the ruler’s virtue is cultivated, the myriad states are set right. Heaven draws close and the people cherish him; his blessings are prolonged forever. He brings glory to his predecessors and leaves a legacy to his successors, flourishing abundantly through unbroken generations.” Our emperor personally puts this into practice. His virtue reaches spirits and human beings alike, bringing harmony above and below, and thus consoles the hearts of his ancestors. And what he hopes of his successors, that they may perpetuate boundless blessings, likewise …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
豈有外于此也哉然爲之有其目焉其心
之所以不敬而德之所以不純者耳目之
欲害之也此四勿之訓所以繼克復而言
而五箴之註在我
皇上不少緩焉是故書過有史不書則非其史
徹膳有宰不徹則非其宰不然僚屬具員
而無保傅之嚴講讀備禮而無箴規之益
宋人臣深慨之可以諸臣見而知之而一
如漢之賈生邪抑愚又有說焉
===
皇上敬一之功自謂因讀書而有得焉而
之末也又惓惓於諸侯卿大夫之亡敬
一以保祿位然後知帝王未嘗廢讀書
宋臣所謂尚書唐史者固正心之功所不
可偏廢而非若唐宋諸君之所謂學云耳
而今日縉紳之士又豈可自謂章句之業
與經綸異使後人慨歎於有君而無臣者
哉草野之臣不知僭妄惟進而教之幸甚
第二問
punctuated:
豈有外于此也哉？然爲之有其目焉。其心之所以不敬，而德之所以不純者，耳目之欲害之也。此四勿之訓所以繼克復而言，而五箴之註，在我皇上不少緩焉。是故書過有史，不書則非其史；徹膳有宰，不徹則非其宰。不然，僚屬具員而無保傅之嚴，講讀備禮而無箴規之益，宋人臣深慨之。可以諸臣見而知之，而一如漢之賈生邪？抑愚又有說焉。
皇上敬一之功，自謂因讀書而有得焉，而之末也，又惓惓於諸侯卿大夫之亡敬一以保祿位。然後知帝王未嘗廢讀書，宋臣所謂《尚書》《唐史》者，固正心之功所不可偏廢，而非若唐宋諸君之所謂學云耳。而今日縉紳之士，又豈可自謂章句之業與經綸異，使後人慨歎於有君而無臣者哉？草野之臣不知僭妄，惟進而教之，幸甚。
第二問
translation_en:
…could it possibly extend beyond this? Yet there are specific means of accomplishing it. The reason the mind lacks reverence and virtue lacks purity is that the desires of the ears and eyes impair them. This is why the teaching of the Four Prohibitions follows the words about overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, and why our Emperor has allowed no delay in annotating the Five Admonitions. Thus, there are scribes to record faults: if they do not record them, they fail as scribes. There are stewards to withdraw dishes: if they do not withdraw them, they fail as stewards. Otherwise, subordinate offices have their full complement of personnel but lack the strictness of guardians and preceptors; lectures and readings observe all the formalities but yield none of the benefits of admonition and correction. A minister of the Song deeply lamented this. Can the ministers perceive and understand this, all becoming like Master Jia of the Han [?]? Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say.
The Emperor himself says that his attainments in reverent oneness came through reading. At the end [of the text?], he again earnestly addresses the failure of the feudal lords, ministers, and great officers to maintain reverent oneness so as to preserve their stipends and positions [?]. From this we understand that emperors and kings have never abandoned reading. The Book of Documents and the History of the Tang mentioned by the Song minister are indeed indispensable to the work of rectifying the mind; neither may be neglected. This is unlike what the rulers of the Tang and Song called learning. How, then, can the gentlemen who hold office today claim that the study of textual divisions and sentences is separate from ordering the affairs of the realm, causing later generations to lament that there was a worthy ruler but no worthy ministers? Your servant, a man of the countryside, is unaware of the presumption and rashness of his words. I would be most fortunate if you would receive me and instruct me.
Second Question

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
尚維詩
考試官教諭童　批〔太甲之業商之所以盛以〕
太甲周莫盛於成王二君先俱無初後卻
克有終其所由致當時全是得伊尹周公二公
志與學其大者伊尹全在伊訓太甲二篇周公
全在無逸立政各篇中大者全是欲王敬德
敷求哲人二事反覆開陳不一而足羞猶
匠之規矩然舍此無所事事者此焉在案
是名臣於此二事皆不先能如伊周□
===
鑿華華務其失之大者益不能致□□
終人德與究已所用者以此當□□□□□
得其細耳此作能語次中多之殆有志於
以幸惠斯民者錄出以益日中
考試官教授趙　批〔保泰之道包荒用馮〕
河不遐遺朋亡得尚于中行士子類知及之
至於帝乙歸妹以祉元吉則無一知之者此
作首能陳到知所力臣知所格君矣
嘗讀易觀聖人所以繫泰六五九二之辭
punctuated:
尚維詩

考試官教諭童，批〔太甲之業商之所以盛以〕：太甲，周莫盛於成王。二君先俱無初，後卻克有終。其所由致，當時全是得伊尹、周公二公志與學。其大者，伊尹全在《伊訓》《太甲》二篇，周公全在《無逸》《立政》各篇中。大者全是欲王敬德、敷求哲人二事，反覆開陳，不一而足，羞猶匠之規矩然，舍此無所事事者。此焉在案，是名臣於此二事皆不先能如伊周□鑿華華務，其失之大者，益不能致□□終人德與究已所用者，以此當□□□□□得其細耳。此作能語次中多之，殆有志於以幸惠斯民者，錄出以益日中。

考試官教授趙，批〔保泰之道包荒用馮〕：河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。士子類知及之。至於「帝乙歸妹，以祉元吉」，則無一知之者。此作首能陳到，知所力臣，知所格君矣。

嘗讀《易》，觀聖人所以繫泰六五、九二之辭。
translation_en:
Shang Weishi

Comment by Examiner Tong, Instructor: 〔“Tai Jia’s undertaking; the reason the Shang flourished …” [?]〕 “… Tai Jia; in the Zhou, none surpassed King Cheng in flourishing achievement. Neither ruler began well, yet both ultimately achieved a good end. What brought this about was entirely their gaining the benefit of the aspirations and learning of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. The essential points of Yi Yin’s teaching are all in the two chapters ‘Instructions of Yi’ and ‘Tai Jia’; those of the Duke of Zhou are all in the chapters ‘Against Ease’ and ‘Establishing Government.’ Above all, they wished the king to attend reverently to virtue and seek wise men far and wide. They repeatedly expounded these two matters in numerous ways. These were like a craftsman’s compass and square [?]; apart from them, there was nothing upon which to apply themselves. The text here concerning eminent ministers and whether they could match Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou in these two matters is doubtful [?]. Preoccupation with ornate embellishment [?] constituted a great failing, making it still less possible to attain … [illegible and garbled text concerning virtue and those employed]. This amounted merely to grasping the minor details [?]. This composition can articulate these matters, with much that hits the mark in its exposition [?]. Its author perhaps aspires to bring blessings and benefits to these people. It is copied out to provide further benefit [?].”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Professor: 〔“The way to preserve peace and prosperity: embracing the uncultivated, employing those who cross …”〕 “… the river on foot, not neglecting the distant, and abandoning factional attachments: thus one may accord with the central course.’ Candidates generally know enough to address this. But as for ‘Di Yi gave his younger sister in marriage, thereby bringing blessing and supreme good fortune,’ not one understands it. This composition is the first able to expound the point fully: its author knows where a minister should exert himself and how to rectify the ruler.”

“I once read the Book of Changes and considered the words that the sage appended to the six in the fifth place and the nine in the second place of the hexagram Tai, ‘Peace,’ …”

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
而知保泰之道責在君臣而於臣爲尤重
也故六五之辭曰帝乙歸妹以祉元吉九
二之辭曰包荒用馮河不遐遺朋亡得尚
于中行夫君之所以君泰者亦何爲哉惟
得夫中行之臣可以任責而代吾事者委
已以聽之則受福而獲吉矣而代君之事
任君之責者忿嫉而隘於量則不足以
容因循而怠於勇則不足以有爲慮不周
而忽於遠則無以□之所由起私不勝而
===
於愛則隱禍之所從生故非有包荒之度
馮河之剛不遐遺之智朋亡之公則不可
尚於中行而中行之克尚聖人猶不輕
以許亭蓋惟如是而後其責塞以能終君
之事而已也是則人之言皆曰爲君難爲
臣不易而未知臣之視君爲尤難也四者
備而尚於中行矣而包荒爲之先聖人之
意豈不以寬裕含弘爲長養民出萬事之
本其明作之剛慮遠之智克鄰之公非此
punctuated: 而知保泰之道，責在君臣，而於臣爲尤重也。故六五之辭曰：「帝乙歸妹，以祉元吉。」九二之辭曰：「包荒，用馮河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。」夫君之所以君泰者，亦何爲哉？惟得夫中行之臣，可以任責而代吾事者，委已以聽之，則受福而獲吉矣。而代君之事、任君之責者，忿嫉而隘於量，則不足以容；因循而怠於勇，則不足以有爲；慮不周而忽於遠，則無以□之所由起；私不勝而於愛，則隱禍之所從生。故非有包荒之度、馮河之剛、不遐遺之智、朋亡之公，則不可尚於中行。而中行之克尚，聖人猶不輕以許亭。蓋惟如是，而後其責塞，以能終君之事而已也。是則人之言皆曰：「爲君難，爲臣不易。」而未知臣之視君爲尤難也。四者備而尚於中行矣，而包荒爲之先。聖人之意，豈不以寬裕含弘爲長養民出萬事之本？其明作之剛、慮遠之智、克鄰之公，非此
translation_en:
…and thus understood that responsibility for preserving peace rests with ruler and ministers, but weighs especially heavily upon the ministers. Hence the statement for the six in the fifth place reads: “Di Yi gave his younger sister in marriage, thereby bringing blessing and supreme good fortune.” The statement for the nine in the second place reads: “Embrace the uncultivated; have the courage to ford a river on foot; do not neglect what is distant; abandon factional attachments: thus may one accord with the central course.” What, then, must a ruler do to preside over peace? He need only obtain a minister who follows the central course, who can bear responsibility and conduct affairs in his stead. If he entrusts himself to that minister and heeds him, he will receive blessings and attain good fortune.

Yet one who conducts the ruler’s affairs and bears his responsibilities cannot be sufficiently accommodating if anger and resentment narrow his capacity. If he merely follows precedent and lacks courage, he cannot accomplish anything. If his deliberations are incomplete and he neglects distant matters, he has no means to [illegible] the source from which trouble arises [?]. If he fails to overcome selfishness and [is partial] in his affections [?], this becomes the source of hidden calamity. Thus, unless he possesses the capacity to embrace the uncultivated, the firmness to ford a river on foot, the wisdom not to neglect what is distant, and the impartiality to abandon factional attachments, he cannot accord with the central course. Even the ability to accord with that course is something the sage does not lightly concede to anyone [?]. Only by being thus equipped can a minister discharge his responsibility and bring his ruler’s affairs to completion—that is all. People all say, “To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy.” Yet they do not understand that being a minister is even more difficult than being a ruler.

With these four qualities complete, one accords with the central course; yet embracing the uncultivated comes first among them. Surely the sage’s meaning is that generosity and broad tolerance form the foundation for nurturing the people and bringing forth all affairs [?]. As for firmness in discerning action, wisdom in considering distant matters, and impartiality in overcoming partiality [?], without this…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
則莫之行也執是以觀則前之所有保護之
責者其得其失必不越乎此矣昔在聖哲
克終厥德惟聖時憲惟臣欽若是故儆戒
無虞罔失法度則舜於羣臣之辭也無教
逸欲兢兢業業則禹臯交勵之道也故天
工時亮庶績咸熙盛德大業蔑以加矣成
湯發葦夏正奄有九有至于太甲回曰之
之治也顛覆典刑敗度敗禮賞罰不中不
矣伊尹勉以毋寺象念惟襄宗而民
===
終允德之美君臣是代大臣以清四海
成王固盛成之運也周公陳戒周公
造當訪予落止矣周公戒以大難詒斯
易惟王而成緝熙光明之學此後世歌大
甲成王之賢而稱伊尹周公之功不衰也
保泰之道孰過于是哉有宋之興英君繼
作仁宗寬明仁恕至誠節儉慶曆之初拔
去羣姦登進衆賢可謂盛矣時則范仲淹
爲之相裁削倖濫考覈賢否以十事條大
punctuated:
則莫之行也。執是以觀，則前之所有保護之責者，其得其失，必不越乎此矣。昔在聖哲，克終厥德，惟聖時憲，惟臣欽若。是故「儆戒無虞，罔失法度」，則舜於羣臣之辭也；「無教逸欲，兢兢業業」，則禹、臯交勵之道也。故天工時亮，庶績咸熙，盛德大業，蔑以加矣。
成湯發葦夏正，奄有九有。至于太甲，回曰之之治也，顛覆典刑，敗度敗禮，賞罰不中，不矣。伊尹勉以毋寺象，念惟襄宗而民，終允德之美。君臣是代，大臣以清四海。成王固盛成之運也。周公陳戒，周公造當訪予落止矣。周公戒以「大難詒斯」，易惟王，而成緝熙光明之學。此後世歌大甲、成王之賢，而稱伊尹、周公之功不衰也。保泰之道，孰過于是哉？
有宋之興，英君繼作。仁宗寬明仁恕，至誠節儉。慶曆之初，拔去羣姦，登進衆賢，可謂盛矣。時則范仲淹爲之相，裁削倖濫，考覈賢否，以十事條大
translation_en:
…then none of these can be put into practice. Viewed in this light, the successes and failures of those in earlier times charged with safeguarding the realm must fall within these principles. The sage rulers of old brought their virtue to fulfillment: the sage provided the model, and his ministers reverently followed it. Thus, “Remain vigilant when there is no cause for alarm, and do not depart from the laws and standards” were Shun’s words to his ministers; “Do not encourage idle pleasures and desires; remain watchful and diligent” expressed the way Yu and Gao [Gao Yao] encouraged one another. Thus Heaven’s work was assisted, all endeavors flourished, and their abundant virtue and great achievements could not be surpassed.
Cheng Tang established his rule in relation to the Xia [?; the wording is garbled] and possessed all the Nine Regions. When it came to Tai Jia, his government [the following wording is garbled: 回曰之之治也] overturned established norms, violated standards and ritual propriety, and imposed inappropriate rewards and punishments [不矣: unclear]. Yi Yin exhorted him [毋寺象: unclear] to give thought to the ancestral line and the people [?], and he ultimately attained the excellence of truly virtuous conduct. Ruler and ministers succeeded one another thus [?], and the great ministers brought order to all within the Four Seas. King Cheng indeed inherited an age of flourishing achievement. The Duke of Zhou presented admonitions [the following passage, 周公造當訪予落止矣, is garbled]. The Duke of Zhou warned him that “great difficulties have been bequeathed here.” [易惟王: unclear.] He thereby perfected his learning in sustained illumination and radiance. This is why later generations have never ceased to celebrate the worthiness of Tai Jia and King Cheng and praise the achievements of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. What could surpass this as a way to preserve peace and prosperity?
With the rise of the Song, outstanding rulers appeared in succession. Renzong was generous and discerning, benevolent and forgiving, utterly sincere and frugal. At the beginning of the Qingli era, he removed the various wicked men and advanced numerous worthy men: this could indeed be called a flourishing age. At that time Fan Zhongyan served as his chief councilor. He curtailed favoritism and abuses and assessed whether men were worthy or unworthy, setting out ten measures in a major…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
章之對以四論救時政之失〔請罷□□□□□〕
德中外想其功業慶曆□□□□之功□□
也王堯臣稱其忠義知勇不當置之散地
呂本中謂本朝人物以仲淹爲第一非溢
美矣然議者猶惜其立朝未久身就退閒
無以成先憂後樂之志何邪蓋古人非無
功之患功而善處之難也仁宗之〔待□之〕
□□□□夫猶在□□也淹□以□□□□
憑河之勇則□□□□□□□□□□
===
□□之計行而河□兩路□□師□□□□
夫朋黨禍作而國以不競〔雖天□□爲□〕
亦人謀之不臧也當時議其規模太闊責
張無漸宣過實之論哉哲宗養德幼冲稟
承母訓元祐之初徵用故老收還遷人亦
可謂盛矣時則司馬光爲之相首開言路
力罷新法弛御前之作息西路之兵天下
鼓舞以觀太平遼夏感服以問起居元祐
punctuated:
章之對，以四論救時政之失〔請罷□□□□□〕。德中外想其功業，慶曆□□□□之功□□也。王堯臣稱其忠義知勇，不當置之散地；呂本中謂本朝人物以仲淹爲第一，非溢美矣。然議者猶惜其立朝未久，身就退閒，無以成先憂後樂之志，何邪？蓋古人非無功之患，功而善處之難也。仁宗之〔待□之〕□□□□夫猶在□□也，淹□以□□□□憑河之勇，則□□□□□□□□□□□□之計行，而河□兩路□□師□□□□夫朋黨禍作，而國以不競〔雖天□□爲□〕，亦人謀之不臧也。當時議其規模太闊，責張無漸，宣過實之論哉？
哲宗養德幼冲，稟承母訓。元祐之初，徵用故老，收還遷人，亦可謂盛矣。時則司馬光爲之相，首開言路，力罷新法，弛御前之作，息西路之兵。天下鼓舞以觀太平，遼夏感服以問起居。元祐
translation_en:
…in his response, and through four discourses sought to remedy the failings of contemporary government. 〔He requested the abolition of [illegible].〕 [The wording concerning his virtue is damaged; ?] Those within and outside the court looked forward to his achievements; the accomplishments of the Qingli era [illegible]. Wang Yaochen praised his loyalty, righteousness, wisdom, and courage, declaring that he should not be relegated to an idle post. Lü Benzhong said that among the notable men of the present dynasty, Fan Zhongyan ranked first. This was no excessive praise. Yet commentators still regretted that, after only a short time at court, he retired into private life, unable to fulfill his aspiration to be first to bear concerns and last to enjoy happiness. Why was this? For the men of old, the concern was not a lack of achievement; the difficulty lay in handling achievement well. Renzong’s [illegible] 〔treatment of [illegible]〕 … still lay in [illegible]. Zhongyan [illegible], with the courage to cross a river on foot [an image of reckless daring], then [illegible] plans were put into effect, and the two circuits of He[?] [illegible passage concerning troops]. The calamity of factional strife arose, and the state consequently lost its strength. 〔Although Heaven [illegible].〕 This, too, resulted from ill-conceived human plans. At the time, critics considered his plans too expansive and reproached him for proceeding without gradual stages. Were these criticisms excessive [?]?
Emperor Zhezong cultivated his virtue while still a child, receiving and following his mother’s instructions. At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, he summoned veteran statesmen into service and recalled men who had been banished. This, too, could be called a flourishing time. Sima Guang then served as his chief councilor. First he opened channels for remonstrance and vigorously abolished the New Policies. He curtailed works undertaken for the emperor and ended military operations on the western front. All under Heaven rejoiced in anticipation of great peace. Liao and Xia, moved to admiration and submission, sent inquiries about the emperor’s well-being. The Yuanyou era …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
之治光之力居多也未盡□□□□活國救□
可謂智仁勇張栻稱其不□論□害近□終
條理非過論矣然議者猶惜其用不及究
業無光顯無以竟旋乾轉坤之功何邪蓋
古人非改作之難改而以其漸之爲貴也哲

包□之量出憑河之勇則非□矣之□其□
□□急於更張怨於講□□由是□□

孔甲率諸儒以歸陳涉，□則甚矣。兩生之賢，獨知幾以長往，雖漢□之興亦不應召，前不從甲，後不從通，何□識之定也！四皓避秦政以隱商山，□□幾矣。老成之年，宜愛身以安，何惠帝一迎
translation_en:
…the Han imperial house. Liu Zhang, an imperial kinsman, acted from within to restrain [illegible] and root out [illegible] partisans [?]. Discerning men admired the greatness of his achievement. Was there not a difference between this and Zhou Bo’s single call to bare the left shoulder, which secured the state? Zhang could prevent trouble before it arose; Bo merely achieved success afterward. If rewards were assessed according to merit, even a fief of a hundred li would have been insufficient for Zhang. Yet Emperor Wen instead gave him lower priority. In this, the Han failed to uphold its established rules of reward.
Zhang Shensu died at the hands of Yang Wang. His son Zhang Xiu lay in ambush and attacked Yang, killing an envoy of the Tang to avenge the injustice done to his father. Commentators [illegible] admired his [illegible] courage [?]. [An illegible passage follows.] For [illegible], on the basis of human feelings [?], the Book of Odes [illegible]. Killing [illegible]. [Further damaged text mentions the Tang, but its meaning is unclear.]
Now, regarding relations between ruler and subject, Zhou Bo fulfilled his loyalty; [the damaged continuation mentions Liu Zhang]. Regarding relations between father and son, Ji Xiu faced the easier circumstances, whereas Zhang Xiu faced the harder ones [illegible]. These are matters to consider when judging loyalty and filial devotion.
Kong Jia led the Confucian scholars in joining Chen She: [the fault referred to in the damaged text] was indeed grave [?]. The two worthy scholars alone discerned the first signs of change and withdrew far away. Even when the Han [illegible] arose, they would not answer its summons. Earlier they had not followed Jia; later they did not follow Tong. How firm their judgment was [illegible]! The Four Hoary Elders withdrew from Qin rule to live in seclusion on Mount Shang, [illegible; apparently referring to their discernment of impending change]. In their advanced years, they ought to have cherished their lives and remained at peace. Why, then, when Emperor Hui invited them just once …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:

正而卒移情於賓客之耽四老自累其書
是出處之當明矣漢明領則〔□□□□□□□〕
乃辭之然君賜臣受禮不爲□而〔□□□□〕
泉語亦未正是特出於矯〔□□□□□□□〕
既見幾而辭師傅之任雖〔□□□□□□□〕
□害於義□武〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
故方孝□〔□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
===
粟助□盡〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
□以濟□〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
所利乎夫均之爲辭□也〔□□□□□□□〕
均之爲尚義也丹也猶式也譎〔□□□□〕
當審矣雖然辯王伯所以審尚也〔□□□〕
謂以德行仁者乎而說道濟私者非矣〔□〕
氣節所以重道也不有所謂剛健中正乎
乎而以亢以屈者非矣譏邪正所以〔□□〕
也不有所謂辟邪距淫者乎而以忿以私
punctuated:
皤然即至，昔則以志，今則以〔□□□□□□□□〕爲也。夫不失身於非類之從〔□□□□□□□□〕正，而卒移情於賓客之耽，四老自累其書，是出處之當明矣。漢明領則〔□□□□□□□〕乃辭之，然君賜臣受，禮不爲□，而〔□□□□〕泉語亦未正，是特出於矯〔□□□□□□□〕既見幾而辭師傅之任，雖〔□□□□□□□〕□害於義，□武〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕故方孝□〔□□□□□□□□□□□□〕粟助□盡〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕□以濟□〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕所利乎？夫均之爲辭□也〔□□□□□□□〕均之爲尚義也，丹也猶式也，譎〔□□□□〕當審矣。

…white-haired, they immediately came. Formerly they acted from conviction; now they acted for [eight illegible characters] reasons [?]. Thus one must clearly understand when to enter service and when to withdraw. “Han Ming ling ze” [?; seven illegible characters] then declined it. Yet for a ruler to bestow and a minister to receive is, according to ritual, not [illegible]; and [four illegible characters] the words concerning “the spring” [?] were also not correct. Having discerned the first signs of change, he declined appointment as tutor; although [seven illegible characters] [illegible] harm to righteousness [illegible] Wu [eleven illegible characters]. Therefore Fang Xiao[illegible] [twelve illegible characters] grain to assist [illegible] exhaust [eleven illegible characters] [illegible] to relieve [illegible] [eleven illegible characters] what benefit was sought [?]? Both alike declined [illegible; seven illegible characters]; both alike esteemed righteousness. Dan, like Shi [?], deceitful [four illegible characters]—this must be carefully examined.

Nevertheless, distinguishing the kingly from the hegemonic way serves to scrutinize what one esteems [three illegible characters]. Does this refer to practicing benevolence through virtue? Those who expound the Way to serve private interests are wrong [one illegible character]. Moral resolve serves to honor the Way. title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
者非矣審義利所以別嫌也不有所謂憙
之與比者乎而以詐以譏者非矣觀忠
所以進德也不有所謂嬰慄篤棐者乎言
以幸以忿者非矣明出處所以脩身也不
有所謂時行時止者乎而以固以隨者非
矣愚生明不足以窮理學未至於正心其
於善惡之微懲勸之故妄有折衷云默之
如此尚有以盡義者惟執事教之
第四問
===
孫科
同考試官訓導張　批〔此篇問目頗繁士子類皆掛漏間有不漏者亦〕〔鮮知折衷此作敘述無遺商確各中情實博而能精者宜冠士〕
同考試官教諭杜　批〔場中策問深以觀士子之學識子於漢以下之賢君并諸儒議論〕〔詳盡末復以上下如須爲言而尤致重於君〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔闡先聖道統一策正以上綽有定見其才識直可謂不負者矣〕
punctuated:
者非矣。審義利，所以別嫌也。不有所謂憙之與比者乎？而以詐以譏者非矣。觀忠，所以進德也。不有所謂嬰慄篤棐者乎？言以幸以忿者非矣。明出處，所以脩身也。不有所謂時行時止者乎？而以固以隨者非矣。愚生明不足以窮理，學未至於正心，其於善惡之微、懲勸之故，妄有折衷，云默之如此。尚有以盡義者，惟執事教之。

第四問
孫科

同考試官訓導張，批〔此篇問目頗繁，士子類皆掛漏，間有不漏者亦〕〔鮮知折衷。此作敘述無遺，商確各中情實，博而能精者，宜冠士。〕

同考試官教諭杜，批〔場中策問，深以觀士子之學識。子於漢以下之賢君并諸儒議論〕〔詳盡，末復以上下如須爲言，而尤致重於君。〕

同考試官教諭李，批〔闡先聖道統，一策正以上綽有定見，其才識直可謂不負者矣。〕
translation_en:
…those who do so are wrong. Examining righteousness and profit serves to distinguish morally questionable cases. Is there not the saying about “delighting in and aligning oneself with it” [?]? Yet those who proceed through deceit or faultfinding are wrong. Considering loyalty serves to advance virtue. Is there not the saying about “awe and earnest assistance” [?]? Those who speak from a desire for undeserved advantage or from anger are wrong. Understanding when to enter office and when to withdraw serves to cultivate oneself. Is there not the saying about acting when it is time to act and stopping when it is time to stop? Yet those who proceed through obstinacy or mere conformity are wrong. My understanding, as an unworthy student, is insufficient to investigate principle fully, and my learning has not yet reached the rectification of the mind. Regarding the subtle distinctions between good and evil and the grounds for discouraging and encouraging conduct, I have presumptuously offered a balanced judgment; my speaking and silence are thus [?]. Whatever remains to be said to expound righteousness fully, I ask you, honored examiners, to teach me.

Fourth Question
Sun Ke

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔This question has numerous parts. Most candidates have omitted something, and even among those who have omitted nothing,〕〔few know how to reach a balanced judgment. This composition leaves nothing out in its account, and its considered judgments each accord with the actual circumstances. Broad yet precise, it deserves to rank first among the candidates.〕

Associate Examiner Du, Instructor, comments: 〔The policy questions in this examination probe deeply into the candidates’ learning and discernment. Your discussion of worthy rulers from the Han onward, together with the arguments of the various Confucian scholars,〕〔is thorough. At the end you return to the mutual dependence of superiors and subordinates [?], placing particular emphasis on the ruler.〕

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔You elucidate the transmission of the Way of the ancient sages. Throughout this policy essay [?], you amply demonstrate settled judgments. Your talent and discernment may truly be said to have fulfilled expectations.〕

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
定國是端學術所繫大有□能又後數陳
卒得其要識高論正其過人遠矣哉
同考試官學正孫　批〔評品古人得失如指諸掌可錄爲斷案〕
考試官教諭童　批〔詳整得體〕
考試官教授趙　批〔明辨有佳士也〕
對大識延促者明治體者也辯醒此者攬
道樞者也□□□□膺執筆以問何辱父爲
雖然敢爰妄言□□□竊論而道之
===
是與經世猶陰□□山□□以尚友
□其理道□□外□□之業可明也□其淵源
而□聖之學可究也且夫天下不可一日
無君也故國統之傳莫之有重□道在天
下未嘗一日亡也故道統之係莫之□有重
焉然驗乎天者脩乎人異其域者同其趨
其延促者其敬怠異其邪其醇疵者其學
詰殊者邪程子曰國祚之祈天永命當
之至于聖賢皆工夫到處□□此應試以
punctuated:
定國是，端學術，所繫大有□能，又後數陳，卒得其要。識高論正，其過人遠矣哉！
同考試官學正孫，批〔評品古人得失，如指諸掌，可錄爲斷案。〕
考試官教諭童，批〔詳整得體。〕
考試官教授趙，批〔明辨有佳士也。〕
對：大識延促者，明治體者也；辯醒此者，攬道樞者也。□□□□膺執筆以問，何辱父爲？雖然，敢爰妄言□□□，竊論而道之。
是與經世猶陰□□山□□以尚友，□其理道□□外□□之業可明也，□其淵源而□聖之學可究也。且夫天下不可一日無君也，故國統之傳莫之有重□；道在天下未嘗一日亡也，故道統之係莫之□有重焉。然驗乎天者，脩乎人；異其域者，同其趨。其延促者，其敬怠異其邪？其醇疵者，其學詰殊者邪？程子曰：「國祚之祈天永命，當之至于聖賢，皆工夫到處□□。」此應試以
translation_en:
…To settle the guiding principles of the state and put learning on a proper footing has great implications [?]. After further repeated exposition [?], he finally grasps the essentials. His insight is lofty and his arguments sound: how far he surpasses others!
Associate Examiner Sun, a School Instructor, comments: “He assesses the successes and failures of the ancients as clearly as if pointing to his own palm. This may be recorded as a definitive judgment.”
Examiner Tong, a School Instructor, comments: “Thorough, orderly, and appropriate.”
Examiner Zhao, a Prefectural School Professor, comments: “Clear discrimination—a fine scholar [?].”
Answer: One who understands the prolongation and shortening [of dynastic rule] understands the essentials of government; one who discerns this clearly [?] grasps the pivot of the Way. [Four illegible characters] taking up the brush to pose questions—why condescend to do so [?]? Nevertheless, I venture to offer these presumptuous words [three illegible characters], privately discussing and explaining the matter.
This, together with ordering the world … mountains … taking the ancients as friends [?]. … Its principles and Way … achievements may be made clear [?]; … its origins, and the learning of the sages may be investigated [?]. Now, all under Heaven cannot be without a ruler for even a single day; hence nothing is weightier than the transmission of dynastic succession [illegible character]. The Way has never ceased to exist under Heaven for even a single day; hence nothing is weightier than maintaining the succession of the Way [text defective]. Yet what is verified in Heaven is cultivated among human beings; what differs in sphere shares the same tendency. Does the prolongation or shortening [of dynastic rule] arise from differences in reverence and negligence [?]? Do purity and flaws arise from differences in learning [?]? Master Cheng said: “As for dynastic longevity, praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate … as for sages and worthies, all depends on the point their efforts have reached [two illegible characters]” [?]. Here, in answering the examination, taking …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
國祚論之唐虞啓運于前夏商周繼昌于
後觀典謨訓誥誓命諸篇固知非盡出
數也蓋亦聖德懋焉自茲以降收功焉
者不事詩書臣虜晉陽者未聞仁義陳橋
之變則冠履倒置天地易位矣然亦易姓
而王天下開基而傳奕世宗祏血食率三
四百年者蓋寬仁大度好謀能聽者負之
以拓統也屬精任賢從諫恤民者寧之以
錫祚也二者欽亦本理也
===
裕也而事之失則亦□事詔有
致者此其□也治其中葉唐以稽遷宋以
震蕩玄宗起自藩邸靖難宮闈理則非不
稔也鑒戒非不近也而離貞觀盛觀覆轍色
荒靈根撼矣高宗遭時不造草昧而侵大
寶憤激非不烈也經略非不開也而制于
姦佞忘親其讎神器危矣至其撥亂反正
號稱中興非以其初政尚善邪然玄宗
哲宗啓躬約復素有姚崇以應變者宋璟
punctuated: 國祚論之，唐虞啓運于前，夏商周繼昌于後。觀典謨訓誥誓命諸篇，固知非盡出數也，蓋亦聖德懋焉。自茲以降，收功焉者不事詩書，臣虜晉陽者未聞仁義，陳橋之變則冠履倒置、天地易位矣。然亦易姓而王天下，開基而傳奕世，宗祏血食率三四百年者，蓋寬仁大度、好謀能聽者負之以拓統也，屬精任賢、從諫恤民者寧之以錫祚也。二者欽亦本理也，裕也，而事之失則亦□事詔有致者，此其□也。治其中葉，唐以稽遷，宋以震蕩。玄宗起自藩邸，靖難宮闈，理則非不稔也，鑒戒非不近也，而離貞觀盛觀，覆轍色荒，靈根撼矣。高宗遭時不造，草昧而侵大寶，憤激非不烈也，經略非不開也，而制于姦佞，忘親其讎，神器危矣。至其撥亂反正，號稱中興，非以其初政尚善邪？然玄宗、哲宗啓躬約復素，有姚崇以應變者，宋璟
translation_en:
…discussing the duration of dynastic rule: Tang and Yu inaugurated their fortunes in antiquity, and Xia, Shang, and Zhou continued to flourish afterward. Reading the chapters comprising canons, counsels, instructions, announcements, oaths, and commands, we certainly know that this did not proceed entirely from predestined allotment; it also owed much to flourishing sagely virtue. Thereafter, those who achieved success did not devote themselves to the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents; those who reduced Jinyang to subjection had not heard of benevolence and righteousness. In the upheaval at Chenqiao, cap and shoes were inverted, and Heaven and Earth exchanged places. Nevertheless, they too changed the ruling surname and ruled All under Heaven, founding dynasties and transmitting them through successive generations. Their ancestral shrines generally received blood offerings for three or four hundred years. This was because rulers who were generous, humane, magnanimous, fond of seeking counsel, and able to listen bore the responsibility of extending their dynastic succession; those who concentrated their energies, employed worthy men, accepted remonstrance, and cared for the people brought stability and thereby secured enduring rule. In both cases, reverence likewise lay at the root of governance and abundance [?]. Yet failures in affairs likewise … brought about consequences [?]; this was their … [?].

In their middle periods, the Tang experienced delay and displacement [?], and the Song experienced upheaval. Xuanzong rose from a princely residence and quelled disorder within the palace. He was hardly unfamiliar with the principles of government, nor were cautionary precedents remote. Yet he departed from the flourishing example of the Zhenguan reign and repeated past mistakes, losing himself in sensual pleasures; the sacred root of his dynasty was shaken. Gaozong encountered an ill-fated age and, amid the unsettled beginnings, encroached upon the imperial throne [?]. His indignation was certainly intense, and his strategic undertakings were by no means undeveloped. Yet he was controlled by treacherous flatterers and forgot his kin and their enemy [?]; the sacred vessel of sovereignty was imperiled. As for their suppression of disorder and restoration of proper rule, acclaimed as a dynastic resurgence, was this not because their early government was still good? Yet Xuanzong and Zhezong personally embraced frugality and returned to simplicity [?]. There was Yao Chong to respond to changing circumstances, and Song Jing …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
以守文高宗秉時應人將士效命守文經營
其內宗澤任其外比其所復也使金□□
國忠秣甫之誤可以無馬嵬之行高宗□
汪黃秦檜之欺可以復廣輪之舊是均之
爲理道者也而理亂異焉是謂驗□□天者
脩乎人非邪以道統論之圖書啟於文義
大成集於宣父觀易書詩春秋禮樂之教
豈不由天縱也然有敏求之學□□自彊以
餘則□□□三年□□□□而□□易
===
其失□□□□□□□□□□勞矣而
未及其失則□扶植人極開世□平□□
無慚德矣而失身仕元大閑已踰□□動
必中律言必稽古名重一時□□山斗者
蓋正義明道高明光大仲舒所□□□□也
深探本原言成一家退之所以不羣也慨
然任道饑渴嗜學平仲所以likely異也一節
或疵難槩論焉執事謂于道未聞恐未
也若夫朱子之學其論存心致知詳矣而

===

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
不足恃也又可知矣幸
聖明在上民心歸戴夷虜運衰而天下無甚旱
戈之警不然則西北既非昔日矣惡在乎
視東南獨爲強壯也哉夫農夫之遇凶歲
與士卒之遇敵其爲國家生民之□□幸則
均爾今天下之農富者已貧貧者已亡斯
其猶士卒之遇敵而北矣而今之士卒則
幸其猶若中歲之農然尚□邊陲之清少
異於□□□□可不動心□之二首
===
爲患□□□□弊或末流□不可□
之於今均不爲迂苟察□此而不以聞□非
國家所以畜養臣下之理與夫有司盡忠之
職分者也是故以漢言之當其開刱之初
建置之用賞賚之優六軍百官之費非不
侈然盛也然流移未盡復夷傷未瘳是時
平原曠野未盡闢也然漕山東之粟以給
京師歲十餘萬石而足則亦何事於海運
武帝時征斂煩苛河渠通利漕益□□
punctuated:
不足恃也，又可知矣。幸聖明在上，民心歸戴，夷虜運衰，而天下無甚旱戈之警。不然，則西北既非昔日矣，惡在乎視東南獨爲強壯也哉？夫農夫之遇凶歲，與士卒之遇敵，其爲國家生民之□□幸則均爾。今天下之農，富者已貧，貧者已亡，斯其猶士卒之遇敵而北矣。而今之士卒，則幸其猶若中歲之農然，尚□邊陲之清，少異於□□□□，可不動心？□之二首爲患□□□□弊，或末流□不可□之於今，均不爲迂。苟察□此而不以聞，□非國家所以畜養臣下之理，與夫有司盡忠之職分者也。
是故，以漢言之，當其開刱之初，建置之用、賞賚之優、六軍百官之費，非不侈然盛也。然流移未盡復，夷傷未瘳，是時平原曠野未盡闢也。然漕山東之粟以給京師，歲十餘萬石而足，則亦何事於海運？武帝時，征斂煩苛，河渠通利，漕益□□
translation_en:
…that the northwest cannot be relied upon is also clear. Fortunately, our sage and enlightened sovereign reigns above; the people give him their allegiance; the fortunes of the foreign foes are declining; and the realm faces no grave alarms of drought or warfare [?]. Otherwise, since the northwest is no longer what it once was, how could one regard the southeast alone as strong and vigorous? When farmers encounter a year of dearth and soldiers encounter an enemy, the implications for the state and its people—their […] fortune [?]—are alike. Among the farmers of the realm today, the rich have become poor, and the poor have perished. This is like soldiers meeting the enemy and fleeing in defeat. The soldiers of today, however, are fortunate still to resemble farmers in an average harvest year. With […] peace on the frontier [?], they differ somewhat from […]. Can this fail to move us? […] two heads [?] causing harm […] abuses, or their subsequent consequences […] cannot […] at present; none of this would be impractical [?]. If one perceives […] this but does not report it, that would […] run counter to the principle by which the state maintains its servants and to the duty of the responsible officials to give their utmost loyalty [?].
Thus, to take the Han as an example: at the beginning of its foundation, expenditure on establishing institutions, lavish rewards, and the costs of the Six Armies and the hundred officials were certainly considerable. Yet the displaced had not all returned, and the wounds of devastation had not healed; at that time, the plains and open lands had not all been brought under cultivation. Nevertheless, grain was transported by water from Shandong to supply the capital, and a little over one hundred thousand shi annually sufficed. What need, then, was there for sea transport? In the time of Emperor Wu, levies were burdensome and harsh, rivers and canals afforded unobstructed passage, and grain transport increasingly […]…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
猶不給也則用度固不在於計歲〔指所之多〕
寡矣今天下晏然無事一歲之入不足以
供一歲之用況可倣漢昭故事一年而盡
免漕也哉夫海運之未可卒通海田之未
可卒置也明矣當旦夕切身之憂而徐思
千百世之計愚固知議之既非其時縱爲
之亦豈可以旦夕就也執事曰唐宋之待
兵數患多而疲耗驕惰〔尤嘗於〕氏固述而
又深〔既〕〔之盜〕盡多寡之數得也於
===
何也夫〔方其〕藩鎮〔之兵半〕天下與
之禁兵爲敵內輕外重之勢正今日之所
宜戒也若宋司馬氏論國初之兵不行比
于英宗時十之一則以當時召募冗濫聚
之于京畿有漢唐之患而無漢唐之利蘇
軾氏已憂其然矣今者兵不加於唐宋而
亦有其患否乎而議者只以清勾而不復
其隊伍之舊爲憂則亦倣韓富二公募民
爲之甚易耳而其見在之數〔執事又復慮〕
punctuated:
猶不給也，則用度固不在於計歲〔指所之多〕寡矣。今天下晏然無事，一歲之入不足以供一歲之用，況可倣漢昭故事，一年而盡免漕也哉？夫海運之未可卒通，海田之未可卒置也，明矣。當旦夕切身之憂，而徐思千百世之計，愚固知議之既非其時，縱爲之，亦豈可以旦夕就也？
執事曰：「唐宋之待兵，數患多而疲耗驕惰〔尤嘗於〕。」氏固述而又深〔既〕〔之盜〕，盡多寡之數，得也於何也？夫〔方其〕藩鎮〔之兵半〕天下，與之禁兵爲敵，內輕外重之勢，正今日之所宜戒也。若宋司馬氏論國初之兵，不行比于英宗時十之一，則以當時召募冗濫，聚之于京畿，有漢唐之患而無漢唐之利，蘇軾氏已憂其然矣。今者兵不加於唐宋，而亦有其患否乎？而議者只以清勾而不復其隊伍之舊爲憂，則亦倣韓富二公募民爲之，甚易耳。而其見在之數〔執事又復慮〕
translation_en:
…still proved insufficient. Expenditure, then, surely does not depend on calculating whether the annual amount is large or small [the small-type annotation here is garbled: “refers to … much” [?]]. Today all under Heaven is peaceful and free of troubles, yet one year's revenue cannot meet one year's expenditure. How, then, could we follow the precedent of Emperor Zhao of Han and exempt everyone from grain transport for an entire year? Clearly, sea transport cannot be opened up immediately, nor can coastal farmland be established immediately. Faced with an urgent anxiety that presses upon us personally, we leisurely contemplate plans for a thousand or a hundred generations. In my humble judgment, such proposals are already untimely; even if undertaken, how could they be completed overnight?
You say: “In maintaining troops, the Tang and Song repeatedly suffered from excessive numbers, exhaustion of resources, arrogance, and indolence.” [The annotation and following text are garbled. They appear to mention someone's account and further examination of troop numbers, then ask how something was obtained [?].] When the troops of the regional military commands occupied half the realm and rivaled the imperial guard forces, the resulting imbalance—a weak center and powerful regions—was precisely what we should guard against today. As for Sima of the Song, he argued that the troops at the dynasty's founding were not even one-tenth as numerous as those under Emperor Yingzong [the wording of the comparison is doubtful [?]]. This was because recruitment at the latter time was excessive and indiscriminate, and the troops were concentrated in the capital region. There were the disadvantages of the Han and Tang systems without their advantages; Su Shi had already expressed concern about this. Today our troops are no more numerous than those of the Tang and Song, but do we nevertheless suffer from the same problems? If those discussing the matter worry only that investigating the military registers and calling up men for service will fail to restore the units to their former strength, then simply following Lords Han and Fu in recruiting civilians for this purpose would be very easy. Yet concerning the numbers actually present [you further worry]…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
其徒有兵之名何哉嗚呼天下之所不可
一日廢者財也而其不得免於用者兵也
二者自古稱國計焉是以聖人未嘗有一
日之乏而猶爲數十年之慮而其於兵也
雖當天下無事之時而常爲有事之憂今
東南爲財賦之藪而其民旣如彼西北爲
戎馬之區而其兵又如此此愚所以謂雖
其爲患有緩急而弊未須於不可救然謀
之於今日不爲迂也事固□□國之
而何□□□勢之□□易□□哉又故
===
賦言之則人皆曰海運不可通也蓋負海諸
郡之粟秦人已致之以攻匈奴矣崔芊之
地可耕也蓋兩浙水田之法虞集已倣而
爲之于元矣而愚以爲此特豐財之說耳
不曰財不可豐去其害財者而已乎不然
而何唐陸贄言之也而宋蘇轍又言之也
贄之言曰能節雖虛必盈不節雖盈必竭
則財固不豐於豐而豐於節者也而求之
punctuated: 其徒有兵之名，何哉？嗚呼！天下之所不可一日廢者，財也；而其不得免於用者，兵也。二者自古稱國計焉。是以聖人未嘗有一日之乏，而猶爲數十年之慮；而其於兵也，雖當天下無事之時，而常爲有事之憂。今東南爲財賦之藪，而其民旣如彼；西北爲戎馬之區，而其兵又如此。此愚所以謂，雖其爲患有緩急，而弊未須於不可救，然謀之於今日，不爲迂也。事固□□國之，而何□□□勢之□□易□□哉？又故賦言之，則人皆曰海運不可通也。蓋負海諸郡之粟，秦人已致之以攻匈奴矣。崔芊之地可耕也，蓋兩浙水田之法，虞集已倣而爲之于元矣。而愚以爲此特豐財之說耳。不曰財不可豐，去其害財者而已乎？不然而何唐陸贄言之也，而宋蘇轍又言之也？贄之言曰：「能節，雖虛必盈；不節，雖盈必竭。」則財固不豐於豐，而豐於節者也。而求之
translation_en:
…why are they soldiers in name alone? Alas! Financial resources are something the realm cannot dispense with for even a single day, while soldiers are something it cannot avoid employing. Since antiquity, these two have been called matters of state finance and planning. Thus, although the sages never lacked supplies for a single day, they still planned for decades ahead; and concerning troops, even when the realm was at peace, they constantly anticipated the troubles of war. Now the southeast is the great source of tax revenue, yet its people are already in the condition described above; the northwest is the region of military activity, yet its troops are likewise in this condition. This is why I humbly maintain that, although these troubles differ in urgency and the abuses have not yet become irreparable [?], planning for them today is no impractical undertaking. Affairs certainly … the state … and how could … the circumstances … easily … [?]

Furthermore, speaking of taxation [?], everyone says that transport by sea is impracticable. Yet the people of Qin already conveyed grain from the coastal commanderies to support their attacks on the Xiongnu. The lands of Cuiqian [?] can be cultivated: during the Yuan, Yu Ji already adopted the wet-field cultivation methods of Liangzhe and put them into practice. But I humbly consider these merely proposals for increasing financial resources. Should we not say that, rather than seeking to increase resources, we need only remove what depletes them? Otherwise, why did Lu Zhi of the Tang say this, and Su Zhe of the Song say it again? Lu Zhi said: “With economy, even empty stores will surely fill; without economy, even full stores will surely be exhausted.” Financial resources thus become abundant through economy in expenditure, rather than through efforts to increase them. And examining this in relation to…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
今日則額外之官世襲之家有可節者乎
賞賚之厚斧斤之役有可已者乎由是實
一分則民受一分之賜矣不然河不足而
又求之海東南沃壤自有不耕之夫而况
京東瀕海之處也哉譬之治生之家方其
窮困時所望不過十金計其平生之費出
入於十金之中而有餘及其少有蓄積則
欲愈廣而財愈不供也即使數十萬粟可
刻期而辦則所有一下若干金焉
===
豐財之說不出此也〔或言之〕
皆曰饑民可募也則富弼嘗行之於京東吾
獨不可行之於兩河乎義勇可刺也則韓
琦行之陝西而民病之吾獨不能處繼輔
之民而使之利之耶而愚以爲此特益兵
之說耳不曰兵貴于精不貴于多者乎不
然而何宋歐陽脩言之也而胡寅又言之
也脩之言曰今所在教習追呼上下主教
者非將領之才所教者無旗鼓之節則多
punctuated:
今日，則額外之官、世襲之家，有可節者乎？賞賚之厚、斧斤之役，有可已者乎？由是實一分，則民受一分之賜矣。不然，河不足而又求之海，東南沃壤自有不耕之夫，而况京東瀕海之處也哉！譬之治生之家，方其窮困時，所望不過十金，計其平生之費，出入於十金之中而有餘；及其少有蓄積，則欲愈廣而財愈不供也。即使數十萬粟可刻期而辦，則所有一下若干金焉。豐財之說不出此也。〔或言之〕
皆曰：「饑民可募也，則富弼嘗行之於京東，吾獨不可行之於兩河乎？義勇可刺也，則韓琦行之陝西而民病之，吾獨不能處繼輔之民而使之利之耶？」而愚以爲此特益兵之說耳。不曰「兵貴于精，不貴于多」者乎？不然而何宋歐陽脩言之也，而胡寅又言之也？脩之言曰：「今所在教習，追呼上下，主教者非將領之才，所教者無旗鼓之節，則多
translation_en:
…today, are there economies to be made in supernumerary offices and hereditary establishments? Can lavish rewards and timber-felling projects be curtailed? Every measure of resources thereby secured brings a corresponding measure of benefit to the people. Otherwise, when river transport proves insufficient, one turns again to the sea. Even on the fertile lands of the southeast there are men who do not cultivate the soil; how much more must this be true along the coast of Jingdong! Consider a household managing its livelihood. When impoverished, it hopes for no more than ten units of gold; reckoning its ordinary expenses, it manages its receipts and outlays within those ten units and still has something left over. Once it has accumulated a little, however, its desires grow ever greater and its resources become ever less adequate. Even if several hundred thousand measures of grain could be procured by a fixed deadline, whatever funds it possessed would be expended at one stroke [?]. Proposals for increasing wealth amount to no more than this. 〔Some speak of it.〕
All say: “Famine victims can be recruited. Fu Bi once did this in Jingdong; could we alone not do it in the Lianghe region? Volunteer militiamen can be tattooed for enlistment. Han Qi carried this out in Shaanxi, and the people suffered from it; could we alone not make arrangements for the people of Jifu [?] that would benefit them?” Yet I, in my humble judgment, regard this merely as a proposal to increase troop numbers. Is it not said, “The value of troops lies in their quality, not their numbers”? Otherwise, why did Ouyang Xiu of the Song say this, and Hu Yin say it again? Xiu said: “In the training now conducted everywhere, men are summoned and driven about at every level. Those directing instruction lack the ability of military commanders, and those receiving it lack discipline in responding to flags and drums. Thus, numerous…”

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
兵非強訓練之有道爲難者也而求之今
日則汰其疲老而歸之耕升其壯健而教
之藝時衣糧之給以厚其生嚴私役之律
以養其力由是得一兵而有一兵之用矣
不然竭天下以養兵見額之數農夫既已
不堪而況又從而益之哉譬之越人有千
金之璧而以與童子童子守之及寇至而後知
童子之無能爲也今天下之兵雖無童不
如越人之童子者□□矣□□兵與練
===
說者□□□□勢既極不變□敗天下
知也爲彼之說策之未必皆非而爲之實
難爲愚之說言之未必皆是而行之實易
夫優至極之勢而迫於旦夕之憂固當自
其易者而先有以處之耳不然則天下之
患豈特此二者而其所當爲者固亦不止
此矣雖然節費所以裕民天下之民譬之
猶羊乎而使狼牧之吾雖欲裕之其誰與
我故長民之吏不可不擇而漢時署伯之
punctuated:
兵非強，訓練之有道爲難者也。而求之今日，則汰其疲老而歸之耕，升其壯健而教之藝，時衣糧之給以厚其生，嚴私役之律以養其力。由是得一兵而有一兵之用矣。不然，竭天下以養兵，見額之數，農夫既已不堪，而況又從而益之哉？譬之越人有千金之璧，而以與童子，童子守之，及寇至，而後知童子之無能爲也。今天下之兵，雖無童不如越人之童子者□□矣，□□兵與練，說者□□□□，勢既極，不變□敗，天下知也。爲彼之說，策之未必皆非，而爲之實難；爲愚之說，言之未必皆是，而行之實易。夫優至極之勢，而迫於旦夕之憂，固當自其易者而先有以處之耳。不然，則天下之患豈特此二者，而其所當爲者固亦不止此矣。

雖然，節費所以裕民。天下之民，譬之猶羊乎，而使狼牧之，吾雖欲裕之，其誰與我？故長民之吏不可不擇，而漢時署伯之
translation_en:
…troops are not thereby strong; the difficulty lies in having the proper method of training them. Applied to the present day, this means dismissing the worn-out and elderly and returning them to farming, promoting the robust and teaching them military skills, supplying clothing and grain on time to sustain their livelihoods, and strictly enforcing the laws against employing soldiers for private service, so as to preserve their strength. In this way, every soldier obtained will provide a soldier’s worth of service. Otherwise, even if all the resources of the realm are exhausted to maintain the army at its existing authorized strength, the farmers already cannot bear the burden. How much less could they bear further increases! It is like a man of Yue who possessed a jade disc worth a thousand pieces of gold and entrusted it to a child. The child guarded it, but only when bandits arrived did the man realize that the child could do nothing. Among the realm’s soldiers today, though there are no children, there are those who are less capable than that child of Yue [?; text damaged]. …troops and training; those advancing proposals… [?; text damaged]. The situation has reached its limit; without change, defeat will follow [?]. Everyone in the realm knows this. As for their proposals, when considered as policy they are not necessarily all wrong, but putting them into practice is truly difficult. As for my humble proposals, what I say is not necessarily all correct, but carrying them out is truly easy. Faced with a situation that has reached its limit [?], and pressed by dangers that may arise at any moment, we should surely begin with what is easy and first take measures to address it. Otherwise, how could the realm’s troubles be confined to these two matters? What ought to be done certainly extends beyond them.

Nevertheless, economizing on expenditure is a means of enriching the people. If the people of the realm are like sheep, and wolves are made to shepherd them, then even though I wish to enrich them, who will assist me? Thus officials who govern the people must be carefully selected; and, in Han times, the … of Shubo [?] …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
殘虐在今日亦有當治而未治者邪数士
所以足兵百萬之師譬之猶狼乎而使羊
將之吾雖欲治兵其誰與我故三軍之將
不可非其人而晚唐債帥之禍在今日亦
有當戒而未戒者乎要之則脩又謂治天
下者雖有憂勤之心而不知致理之西則
心愈勞而事愈乖而琦亦欲宋之先治內
患以去外憂其言具在宋史可攷也使二
子而見□□□則可不然則□事所問
===
謂今日□有之矣而愚所□琦不謂
之慮皆能及之也乎迂儒之言惟執事諒
其心而不罪其僭幸矣敢自附于范希文
之後也哉
punctuated: 殘虐，在今日亦有當治而未治者邪？数士所以足兵，百萬之師譬之猶狼乎，而使羊將之，吾雖欲治兵，其誰與我？故三軍之將不可非其人，而晚唐債帥之禍，在今日亦有當戒而未戒者乎？要之，則脩又謂治天下者，雖有憂勤之心，而不知致理之西，則心愈勞而事愈乖；而琦亦欲宋之先治內患，以去外憂。其言具在宋史，可攷也。使二子而見□□□，則可；不然，則□事所問，謂今日□有之矣。而愚所□琦不謂之慮，皆能及之也乎？迂儒之言，惟執事諒其心，而不罪其僭，幸矣！敢自附于范希文之後也哉？
translation_en:
…cruelty: are there likewise instances today that ought to be dealt with but have not been? Counting the men [?] is the means of ensuring sufficient military strength. An army of a million may be likened to wolves; if sheep are appointed to command them, then, though I wish to put the army in order, who will assist me? Thus, the commander of the armies must be the right man. As for the calamity of the late Tang commanders who incurred debts to purchase their commands, are there likewise things today against which precautions ought to have been taken but have not?

In sum, Xiu 脩 also said that those who govern the realm, though concerned and diligent, may not understand the means [?] of bringing about good government: the more they weary their minds, the further affairs go awry. Qi 琦 likewise wished the Song first to remedy its internal troubles so as to remove its external anxieties. Their words are all recorded in the History of the Song and can be consulted. If these two men were to see □□□, then it would be possible; otherwise, as for what □ asks, it is said that today □ exists. Yet could all have encompassed the concerns that I □ and that Qi did not speak of [?]?

These are the words of an impractical scholar. I would count myself fortunate if you would understand my intentions and not condemn my presumption. How could I dare to place myself among the followers of Fan Xiwen 范希文?

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試録後序
序曰自昔君子之大有建立
於天下也良不偶焉其初也
恒由養以充之其終也未嘗
不因於所遇以玉其成猶之
木然長養於山林之中雨露
之所膏潤煙霞之所披拂非
===
不材然秀穹然大也而柯幹
柔脆任重不力匠石者無取
焉遲之以歲時而卒遇霜雪
過之嚴凝寒凓之氣迭相摧
剝使其堅實挺直斯可登而
材也故一出而堪棟梁之用
以壯夫廟堂之觀吁亦難哉
punctuated:
河南鄉試録後序

序曰：自昔君子之大有建立於天下也，良不偶焉。其初也，恒由養以充之；其終也，未嘗不因於所遇以玉其成。猶之木然，長養於山林之中，雨露之所膏潤，煙霞之所披拂，非不材然秀、穹然大也，而柯幹柔脆，任重不力，匠石者無取焉。遲之以歲時，而卒遇霜雪，過之嚴凝寒凓之氣，迭相摧剝，使其堅實挺直，斯可登而材也。故一出而堪棟梁之用，以壯夫廟堂之觀。吁，亦難哉！
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

The postface says: From antiquity, the great achievements established by gentlemen in the world have indeed never come about by chance. At the outset, they invariably develop their capacities through cultivation; in the end, the circumstances they encounter invariably bring them to perfection, as jade is polished. It is like a tree growing amid mountain forests, nourished by rain and dew and brushed by mist and cloud. It may grow fine [?], lofty, and large, yet if its branches and trunk are soft and brittle, unable to bear a heavy load, a master carpenter such as Shi will find no use for it. Give it years and seasons, however, and it will eventually encounter frost and snow. The bitter, freezing cold passing over it repeatedly batters and strips it, making it firm, sound, upright, and straight. Only then can it be selected and used as timber. Thus, once brought forth, it is fit to serve as a ridgepole or beam, lending grandeur to the court’s halls. Ah, how difficult this is!

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南昔稱多賢之地名德碩
輔自二程司馬而下未易縷
數以今觀之曾有一之不由
此其選邪夫急小成者無以
與於遠大之規懷安便者終
不能勝於負荷之任此無他
無所於激而發士之不立而
===
氣餒焉故也天下之事孰不
藉氣以有成哉集義深者其
氣大以剛更事多者其氣闊
以定艱苦備嘗者其氣厲以
烈世而有大經綸大建置焉
其必自此人爲之茲觀於諸
士子之文也談經者覈其眞
punctuated: 河南昔稱多賢之地，名德碩輔，自二程、司馬而下，未易縷數。以今觀之，曾有一之不由此其選邪？夫急小成者，無以與於遠大之規；懷安便者，終不能勝於負荷之任。此無他，無所於激而發，士之不立而氣餒焉故也。天下之事，孰不藉氣以有成哉？集義深者，其氣大以剛；更事多者，其氣闊以定；艱苦備嘗者，其氣厲以烈。世而有大經綸、大建置焉，其必自此人爲之。茲觀於諸士子之文也，談經者覈其眞，
translation_en: Henan has long been called a land of many worthies. Its men renowned for virtue and its eminent ministers, from the two Cheng brothers and Sima onward, cannot readily be enumerated. Viewed from the present, was there ever one who attained distinction without undergoing such selection? Those impatient for small accomplishments cannot participate in plans of far-reaching scope; those who cherish ease and convenience can never shoulder weighty responsibilities. This is for no other reason than that, having nothing to stir them into action, scholars fail to establish themselves [?] and their vital spirit falters. What undertaking in the world can succeed without relying on this spirit? In those who have profoundly accumulated righteousness, it is vast and firm; in those who have experienced many affairs, it is broad and steady; in those who have tasted every hardship, it is vigorous and ardent. If there are great achievements in ordering the world and establishing its institutions, surely it is such men who accomplish them. Now, examining the writings of these examination candidates, I find that those who discuss the Classics scrutinize their true meaning…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
論史者摘其要洋洋乎二程
氏之遺也然猶其肄業及之
者非其至焉利病之稱述如
其身親見之政理之敷陳即
今日而可推之行事洸洸乎
司馬氏之略也然猶其見與
之有考者亦非不焉乃於文
===
字之外詳而玩之則見其壯
槩相先奇氣可挹上焉者剛
毅以正直前有爲如馳駿足
於萬里之程不論嶮夷而勢
必達又如植以擎天之柱不
問重與輕而負戴之其次則
肅然特立不與物俯仰或脩
punctuated: 論史者摘其要，洋洋乎二程氏之遺也。然猶其肄業及之者，非其至焉。利病之稱述，如其身親見之；政理之敷陳，即今日而可推之行事，洸洸乎司馬氏之略也。然猶其見與之有考者，亦非不焉。乃於文字之外詳而玩之，則見其壯槩相先，奇氣可挹。上焉者剛毅以正，直前有爲，如馳駿足於萬里之程，不論嶮夷而勢必達；又如植以擎天之柱，不問重與輕而負戴之。其次則肅然特立，不與物俯仰，或脩
translation_en: …those discussing history select its essentials: how abundantly they display the legacy of the two Cheng masters! Yet this is still something attained through their studies, not their highest achievement. They describe benefits and harms as though they had witnessed them personally; they expound principles of government that could be put into practice this very day. How impressive is their grasp of statecraft in the tradition of Master Sima! Yet this is still a matter of their views having a basis for verification [?]; the following phrase, “also is not not so,” is unclear [?]. Looking beyond the written words and pondering them closely, one sees their heroic bearing, each striving to surpass the others, and an extraordinary spirit that one can imbibe. The best among them are firm, resolute, and upright, advancing straight ahead to accomplish things, like swift steeds galloping on a journey of ten thousand li: whether the ground is rugged or level, their momentum ensures that they will arrive. They are also like pillars erected to support the heavens, bearing their burdens regardless of whether these are heavy or light. Those next in rank stand solemnly independent, neither bowing nor rising with external circumstances; others are lofty …

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
然清遠不比於俗斯皆天下
之正氣也夫以氣焉如是志
固有在矣志焉如是即事業
可知矣諸士子養於學校之
中詩禮優游絃歌上下道非
所以致此也而有是氣何哉
噫有日矣間者河南比歲不
===
登茀已相望者經乎百餘州
縣又屬有賊盜之變兵戈之
擾至屢
聖天子遣使賑恤之士生斯際厥
惟艱哉窮阨流離之狀呻吟
愁慼之聲非其親姻則其里
閈又多有躬自罹之者其所
punctuated:
然清遠，不比於俗，斯皆天下之正氣也。夫以氣焉如是，志固有在矣；志焉如是，即事業可知矣。諸士子養於學校之中，詩禮優游，絃歌上下，道非所以致此也，而有是氣何哉？噫！有日矣。
間者河南比歲不登，茀已相望者經乎百餘州縣，又屬有賊盜之變、兵戈之擾，至屢聖天子遣使賑恤之。士生斯際，厥惟艱哉！窮阨流離之狀，呻吟愁慼之聲，非其親姻，則其里閈，又多有躬自罹之者。其所
translation_en:
…pure and aloof, refusing to conform to vulgar ways: these are all manifestations of the upright vital force of the realm. With such vital force, their aspirations surely have a firm direction; with such aspirations, their future accomplishments can already be discerned. These students have been nurtured in the schools, dwelling at ease amid poetry and ritual, advancing and retreating amid strings and song. The Way is not what brings this about [?]; how, then, have they come to possess such vital force? Ah! It has been developing for some time.
Recently, Henan has suffered successive years of failed harvests. Weed-choked fields [?] have stretched one after another across more than a hundred subprefectures and counties. On top of this have come outbreaks of banditry and the disturbances of warfare, to the point that the sagely Son of Heaven has repeatedly dispatched envoys to provide relief. How difficult it has been for scholars living through these times! The sights of destitution and displacement, the sounds of groaning and grief—if these did not come from their relatives by blood or marriage, they came from their neighbors. Many have also suffered these hardships themselves. What they…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
以消磨其優閑之習而立之
懦激發風流以起其高者固
於摧挫困抑中得之此氣志
之所以異於曩時而將來之
待者也豈不猶楩楠豫章
剝於霜雪以就其大材與
曰天上之民不𥘉□之膏
===
之□莫不向義𥘉世方其
徵矣昔傅說之相也以傅
膠鬲之舉也以魚鹽管夷
之用也以士苦其心志勞
筋骨空乏其身而拂亂
將動其心性益其所不能以
降之大任爾矣從古賢聖豪
punctuated:
以消磨其優閑之習，而立之懦，激發風流，以起其高者，固於摧挫困抑中得之。此氣志之所以異於曩時，而將來之待者也。豈不猶楩楠豫章剝於霜雪，以就其大材與？
曰：天上之民不𥘉□之膏之□，莫不向義𥘉世，方其徵矣。昔傅說之相也以傅，膠鬲之舉也以魚鹽，管夷之用也以士。苦其心志，勞筋骨，空乏其身，而拂亂，將動其心性，益其所不能，以降之大任爾矣。從古賢聖豪
translation_en:
…thereby wearing away their habits of comfortable leisure, strengthening the timid [?], stirring their spirit, and elevating their aspirations: these gains assuredly came amid setbacks and hardship. This is why their spirit and resolve differ from former times, and why expectations are placed upon their future. Are they not like the great trees pian, nan, and yuzhang, stripped by frost and snow so that they may become timber of great worth?
It is said: “The people of Heaven …” [the passage containing 𥘉□之膏之□ is garbled]. None fails to turn toward righteousness [?]; here is the evidence. Formerly, Fu Yue became chief minister through Fu [?]; Jiao Ge was raised to office from the fish and salt trade; Guan Yi [?] was employed after passing through the hands of a judicial officer. Their hearts and wills were afflicted, their sinews and bones wearied, their persons subjected to deprivation, and their undertakings thwarted and thrown into disorder—all to stir their hearts and natures, increase their capacities, and confer great responsibilities upon them. From antiquity, worthy men, sages, and outstanding figures…

title: 嘉靖十九年河南鄉試錄
text:
傑皆以得所遇而𤣥其成今
諸士既同其遇矣自茲以往
尚其持此初志以無餒其□□
使可以登用於
國家弘濟於生民則今日加
之意也夫如傳說膠鬲者
一人而猶足以□
===
數人□有並□
以張矣豈非主司
於戲豈非主司者
江西饒州府樂平縣
諭童珂謹序
punctuated:
傑皆以得所遇而𤣥其成。今諸士既同其遇矣，自茲以往，尚其持此初志，以無餒其□□，使可以登用於國家，弘濟於生民，則今日加之意也。夫如傳說、膠鬲者，一人而猶足以□數人，□有並□以張矣，豈非主司？於戲！豈非主司者？
江西饒州府樂平縣諭童珂謹序。
translation_en:
…outstanding men all attained their accomplishments [?] by meeting with a fitting opportunity. Now you gentlemen have alike encountered such an opportunity. Henceforth, may you maintain this original resolve, without allowing your □□ to flag, so that you may be appointed to serve the state and bring extensive relief to the people. Such is the intention behind what has been conferred today [?]. For men such as Fu Yue 傳說 [?] and Jiao Ge 膠鬲, even one alone was sufficient to □ several men [?]; □ together there were □ to extend [their influence?]. Was this not the responsibility of those presiding over the examination [?]? Alas! Was it not those presiding over the examination [?]?
Preface respectfully composed by Tong Ke 童珂, Instructor [?] of Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
